https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/sto.text: Influencer brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested Saturday in Miami after U.K. prosecutors said they brought additional rape and sex trafficking charges against them. Britain's Crown Prosecution Service said the new charges relate to four further victims and were brought after authorities received evidence from Bedfordshire Police in southeastern England. The charges include rape, assault, trafficking and offenses relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.” The charges announced Saturday, which bring the total number of alleged victims in the U.K. to seven, are the latest in a long-running international legal saga involving the brothers that has spanned the United States, Britain and Romania. The brothers have denied wrongdoing. Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, are dual U.S.-British citizens known for their social media empire promoting wealth, male dominance and misogyny. Andrew Tate is a former professional kickboxer and self-described misogynist who has amassed more than 10 million followers, most of them boys and young men, on X. He has been banned from platforms including YouTube, TikTok and Instagram for violating hate speech guidelines. He also runs an online academy where he says he teaches young men how to get rich and attract women. Tristan Tate is also a former kickboxer. The brothers are avid supporters of President Trump. The Tates have faced multiple charges in the U.K. and Romania, where they moved in 2016. British prosecutors said the new charges relate to alleged offenses that took place between 2010 and 2017. They said Andrew Tate was charged with seven additional counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault and 19 charges for offenses relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate was charged with one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating sex trafficking. The Crown Prosecution Service said in a statement it “has requested the extradition of the Tates from the U.S. They have been arrested and await extradition proceedings to the U.K.” The Tates already face previous charges of rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other alleged victims in the U.K. between 2012 and 2015. In June, a U.K. High Court judge threw out a legal bid by the Tates to be told the names of their accusers. In Romania, the siblings were arrested in late 2022 along with two Romanian women. The four were accused of participating in criminal schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations, and the Romanian case hasn’t gone forward because of legal and procedural problems. The case hasn’t been closed, and there is also a separate legal case against the brothers in Romania. Andrew Tate has repeatedly claimed that prosecutors in Romania have no evidence against him and that there is a political conspiracy to silence him. The brothers are expected to appear this week in a U.S. federal court, where a judge will make an initial determination about whether they meet the conditions for extradition. If they do, they are unlikely to get bail, which is rarely granted to those held for international extradition. The decision about whether to order the extradition will then fall to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. While the State Department has some discretion to deny extradition requests from the U.K., it has granted nearly every British request since ratifying a strengthened extradition treaty in 2007. One exception came during Trump’s first term, when the U.S. declined an extradition request for the wife of a former American diplomat involved in a fatal crash in England, citing diplomatic immunity. The rejection prompted an international outcry. British police previously sought the Tates' extradition to the U.K. once their legal proceedings in Romania concluded. But in February 2025 they were allowed to leave Romania after authorities lifted travel restrictions, and they flew to Florida on a private jet. Romania's foreign minister said at the time that a U.S. official in the Trump administration had expressed interest in the brothers’ legal case in Romania. Trump said he knew “nothing about” the case when asked if his administration pressured the Romania government to release the Tates. Hui writes for the Associated Press.

https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/focus/break.text: BIG DREAMS:The education ministry said it hoped that by hosting the competition next year, it could help Taiwan nurture talented students and foster global connectionsBy Fion Khan / Staff writer, with CNA請繼續往下閱讀...Taiwanese high-school students over the weekend swept four gold medals at the International Biology Olympiad （IBO） in Lithuania, and secured three golds and one silver at the International Chemistry Olympiad （IChO） in Uzbekistan.All four members of the Taiwan team for IBO — Hsu Ting-jui （許庭睿） from Taichung First Senior High School, Chen Yu-chen （陳語晨） from Taipei First Girls’ High School, and Chan Wei-chun （詹緯濬） and Yao Yi-keng （姚亦耕） from Taipei Municipal Chien Kuo High School — received gold medals in the competition, which was held from Sunday last week to yesterday, the Taiwanese Representative Office in Lithuania said in a statement.Representative to Lithuania Constance Wang （王雪虹） passed on congratulatory messages from President William Lai （賴清德） and Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim （蕭美琴） to the students at the awards ceremony, praising their exceptional performances and encouraging them to continue honing their expertise to shine in their respective fields, the office said.The IBO is one of the premier biology competitions for high-school students and drew more than 300 students from 78 countries this year, it said, adding that Taiwan has participated in the IBO since 1999 and has consistently achieved good results.Meanwhile, the K-12 Education Administration said Taiwan ranked third globally at the IChO after bagging three gold medals and one silver.The three gold medalists are Fang Yi-chen （方怡宸） from Chien Kuo High School, Chang Chen-jui （張宸睿） from Kaohsiung Senior High School and Fan Yi-yang （范奕揚） from Taichung First Senior High School, it said,Cheng Ping-hao （鄭秉皓） from the National Experimental High School at Hsinchu Science Park took home the silver medal, it added.The four students were selected from 2,406 applicants across 141 schools nationwide through a rigorous four-stage process that was overseen by a panel of more than 10 university professors, it said.Taiwan has been an active participant of the IChO since 1992 and is set to host the 59th edition of the competition next year, the agency said, adding that the Taiwanese team received the tournament flag during the closing ceremony to bring back to Taiwan.The Ministry of Education said it hoped that hosting the international competition next year would provide Taiwan with another international stage to discover and nurture talented students in science and mathematics through fostering global connections.新聞來源：TAIPEI TIMES

SAME GOALS: Taiwan’s and Germany’s memorial sites all aim to transform spaces of injustice to sites that advance human rights, said the minister’s guide, Sebastian KornerBy Huang Ching-hsuan / Staff reporter請繼續往下閱讀...Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung （林佳龍） in a Facebook post yesterday revealed that he had visited Germany last month and toured the Berlin Wall and the Berlin-Hohenschonhausen Memorial, among other sites.This year marks the 39th anniversary of the lifting of martial law in Taiwan, surpassing the 38-year duration of martial law, he wrote.Martial law was imposed on May 20, 1949, and lifted on July 15, 1987.“From the lifting of martial law and removal of bans on political parties and newspapers, to having direct elections for legislators and the president, Taiwan has little by little stepped out of the shadow of authoritarian rule to become the free, democratic and open country it is today,” Lin wrote.“The free air we breathe today and take for granted was fought for step by step by many democratic pioneers who used their courage, sacrifice and perseverance during a time of forced silence,” he said, adding that having been a democratic activist on campus, he appreciates Taiwan’s hard-won democracy and cherishes it.Lin wrote about his visit to Germany, including trips to the Berlin Wall and the Hohenschonhausen Memorial, a former prison used by the East German Ministry for State Security （“Stasi”） to hold political prisoners.A man named Sebastian Korner, a family member of a victim of political persecution, guided him through the memorial, from freezing cells and interrogation rooms to prisoner transport vehicles, he said.The Stasi had deployed a vast intelligence network across Germany to spy on its citizens, Lin said.It utilized isolation, intimidation and psychological torture to strip detainees of their sense of time and direction, further breaking their will and allowing authoritarian rule to penetrate every corner of people’s lives, he said.Lin said he talked with Korner about Taiwan’s White Terror history and ongoing efforts to push forward transitional justice, and recommended he watch the movie A Foggy Tale （大濛） to better understand Taiwanese’s suffering during martial law.After returning to Taiwan, Lin said he received a letter from Korner telling him that he looked up information on Taiwan and found that the Hohenschonhausen Memorial serves a similar mission as Taiwan’s Jing-Mei White Terror Memorial Park （白色恐怖景美紀念園區） and Green Island White Terror Memorial Park （白色恐怖綠島紀念園區） — transforming spaces of historical injustice into key sites that preserve memories, uncover the truth and advance human rights education, Lin said.“I also hope to have the opportunity to invite Sebastian to Taiwan in the future, to engage in exchanges on human rights education and transitional justice,” he said. “Germany and Taiwan have experienced different histories of authoritarian rule, but share a common understanding — only by revealing the truth, restoring dignity to victims and using history to educate the next generation on human rights can democracy endure and hard-won freedom be passed down.”Lin had led a delegation to attend the opening of the Taiwan Expo in Europe in Warsaw on June 22, visited the Polish Parliament on June 23, and on June 24 announced plans to establish language centers in Europe, starting in the Czech Republic, France, Germany and Poland.Lin’s trip to Germany marks another significant trip to Berlin by Taiwanese officials over the past few years. National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu （吳釗燮） visited Germany in June last year, when the German Marshall Fund of the US invited him to attend the Taiwan Trilateral Forum.Wu delivered a keynote speech during the event.He also talked to German lawmakers and European policy experts on issues such as Taiwan Strait security, cooperation among democratic partners, supply chain resilience and challenges posed by the expansion of authoritarian regimes.Sources familiar with the matter said European partners have shown interest in potential cooperation with Taiwan in emerging technology areas such as uncrewed aerial vehicles and artificial intelligence. Additional reporting by Lee I-chia and CNA新聞來源：TAIPEI TIMES

https://www.irishdentist.ie/grandmas-gol.text: Politics July 19, 2026 Grandma’s gold is worth a fortune: the wealth hidden in Italian homes The big bankers on Wall Street spend their days interrogating algorithms as intricate as a charade. Global financial strategists chase artificial intelligence, supercomputers and mysterious market movements. To power his gigantic data centers, Jeff Bezos even goes hunting for copper underground in Arizona, with the spirit of a Klondike gold prospector wearing the helmet of a technological entrepreneur. In Italy, however, the nation’s sovereign wealth fund, the one that preserves the country’s wealth, is within reach. You don’t need to dig mountains, you don’t need drills, you don’t even need an ultra-fast internet connection. Just open the dresser drawer. Yes, exactly that. The sacred place where mismatched socks, old supermarket receipts, faded photographs and, often, a small forgotten heritage coexist: the grandmother’s necklace, the baptism bracelet, the brooch given by the aunt, the ring preserved in a velvet box now worn out by time. A treasure which according to estimates, the reliability of which is difficult to verify, could be worth 150 billion. For years we looked at him with a mixture of tenderness and sufficiency. Objects from the past, memories of an Italy made up of family ceremonies, communions, confirmations and weddings. Grandpa stuff, we thought. A bit like the doilies on the television and the wedding favors with the music box. Then the gold market came to remind us of a truth: the yellow metal has a much longer memory than ours. At the beginning of the year, gold touched unthinkable levels, exceeding 5,500 dollars an ounce. Silver also experienced an extraordinary run, reaching above 116 dollars. Now the wind has changed: gold has fallen to around 4,100 dollars an ounce and silver has plummeted towards 61 dollars. An important slowdown, but not enough to erase an impressive growth story. Because ten years ago the yellow metal was trading around 30-32 euros per gram. Today we are around 116 euros per gram for the pure one. In short, that hair-thin chain that seemed like a gift of no great importance could today have a value capable of paying a few bills or a few tanks of petrol. In short, the aunt with the white hair and the impeccable skirt perhaps had understood everything before the Wall Street analysts. The great revenge of gold concerns above all those objects that have remained forgotten for decades. Baptism necklaces. Milan knitted bracelets. Earrings passed down from mother to daughter. Those pins with initials that seemed destined to lie forever inside a jewelry box. Today those little pieces of family have a new life. Gold does not need software updates, does not fear hackers, does not require complicated passwords. It doesn’t need artificial intelligence to remind us of its value. He sits there, still, maybe for twenty years, patiently waiting for someone to notice him. And it’s not just the jewels. There is an entire universe of coins that has rediscovered a second youth. The pound, that currency that grandparents bought “for safety”, is today worth around 850-900 euros. A small disc of precious metal which for many seemed just a whim for nostalgic collectors and which today can instead be transformed into a cruise or a nice paid bill. Then there is the Marengo, the 20 franc or 20 lire coin that smells of Napoleonic history. Today its value is around 700 euros. And even the old 500 lire silver Caravelle, the ones with Christopher Columbus’ ships pushed by the wind, have regained their dignity. Common examples are worth around ten euros, but the very rare 1957 version with the “against the wind” flags, which never came into circulation due to the error in the minting, can reach collector’s figures of up to thousands of euros: from 3 thousand to 12 thousand. A sort of “Gronchi Rosa” of Italian numismatics given that the sails are inflated by the wind in the opposite direction to the bow. In short, while technology promises us a future made up of augmented reality and virtual worlds, the past hidden in drawers continues to produce real value. Now this hidden wealth finds a new home: the stock market. The protagonist is Gens Aurea, European leader in regenerated gold, owner of brands such as Orocash, GioiaPura and Luxury Zone. The company became the protagonist of the first major IPO on Piazza Affari after about three years. An important signal: the market is once again looking for true industrial stories, even when they arise from an ancient sector like that of gold. The operation aims to value the group at around 1.4 billion euros and represents a strategic step to accompany international growth. Gens Aurea is not simply an advanced gold buyer. It is an integrated platform that buys used precious stones, recovers them, refines them and returns them to the jewelery supply chain. The group has over 530 stores in Europe and in 2025 recorded 836 million euros in revenues, 105 million in adjusted Ebitda and 68 million in net profit. The objectives are even more ambitious: 1.5 billion in revenues, over 200 million in gross margin and more than 130 million in net profit are expected for 2026. The industrial plan envisages reaching over 750 stores by 2029, with strong expansion in Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, Poland and Romania. CEO Fabio Godano summarizes the challenge thus: «We have built a unique platform in the European gold and precious objects market, becoming the largest operator in the regenerated gold sector in Europe. Our platform integrates a widespread presence in retail, industrial expertise, digital skills and rigorous compliance monitoring.” For Godano, the listing represents a natural step to support growth: «We have a plan for 300 new stores in the next three years. A significant portion of our growth will come from our ability to open stores quickly and efficiently.” In short, the future also depends on being able to transform grandmother’s old jewel into a new raw material. The other side of the coin is called Kruso Kapital. Here gold is used as collateral to obtain liquidity. The company was founded in 2017 when Banca Sistema entered the pawn credit sector with the ProntoPegno brand. The goal was to completely change the perception of an ancient activity, often associated with difficult moments in life. The modern version of the pawnshop instead becomes a financial tool for families. In 2022 comes the change of name and a new strategy: to enhance not only jewelery and watches, but also works of art and collectibles. Kruso Art is born, with the acquisition of the Art-Rite auction house, while the Art-Kredit project paves the way for loans guaranteed by works of art. Growth becomes international: Italy, Greece and Portugal. In 2024 the company acquired Pignus, a historic Portuguese pawnbroker. After listing on EGM in 2024, Kruso Kapital made the leap to the main market in 2026. CEO Giuseppe Gentile has explained several times that pawn credit should not be considered an emergency product, but a modern financial service. No longer “I wear the ring because I’m in difficulty”, but “I enhance an asset that I own without having to sell it”. On the occasion of the transition to the main list, Gentile defined the operation: «A natural evolution of the company’s path, destined to increase transparency, visibility and credibility towards investors and customers». In the end the moral is simple. While the world rushes towards cryptocurrencies, artificial intelligence and virtual realities, Italians are rediscovering an ancient heritage. The real national sovereign wealth fund is not hidden in large financial databases. It’s in the drawers with the laundry. Inside those forgotten boxes where a farsighted grandmother had placed a necklace, a coin, a bracelet. Small objects, often considered outdated, which today become protagonists again. Because gold can go down, it can correct, it can take a break. But it has a quality that few investments possess: it knows how to wait. And sometimes, after years of gathering dust, it reminds us of how much it is worth. Acțiune Facebook X WhatsApp Telegram VK The Moinești Local Council voted on Thursday to end the mandate of Professor Adrian Cotîrleț , director of the Moinești Clinical Emergency Municipal Hospital, bringing to a close more than two decades of leadership during which the institution became one of Romania’s most highly regarded public hospitals. The decision was approved by 11 members of the Local Council during an extraordinary meeting. The session took place amid heightened tensions, with around 300 hospital employees gathering outside the council chamber and attending the meeting to express support for Cotîrleț. Staff members argued that his dismissal could undermine the hospital’s stability and future development. Moinești Mayor Valentin Vieru said the decision was not a reflection of Cotîrleț’s professional achievements but was instead required by legal provisions governing the tenure and eligibility of public hospital managers. According to the mayor, the current management contract had already been extended, and local authorities were obliged to comply with legislation concerning age limits and the conditions for remaining in office. Cotîrleț, widely regarded as one of Romania’s most successful hospital managers, has led the institution since 2001 . During his tenure, the hospital evolved from a small municipal facility with limited resources into a regional medical center attracting patients from across Romania and frequently cited as a model of best practice in hospital management. In recent years, the institution became the Moinești Clinical Emergency Municipal Hospital , earning clinical hospital status despite not being affiliated with one of Romania’s traditional university medical centers. It has secured significant investments in infrastructure and medical equipment, implemented numerous European-funded projects, and developed several centers of medical excellence. The hospital also hosts the Moinești Medical Days , an annual scientific conference considered among Romania’s leading medical events. Earlier this year, the Romanian Academy of Scientists awarded Cotîrleț its Diploma of Excellence and Gold Medal on the occasion of his 70th birthday, recognizing his contributions to Romanian medicine and hospital management. The Local Council’s decision marks one of the most significant leadership changes in Bacău County’s healthcare system in recent years, affecting an institution that has earned national recognition for its medical performance and managerial achievements under Cotîrleț’s leadership. https://www.easternmirrornagaland.com:44.text: Nagaland Districts Chümoukedima Dimapur Kiphire Kohima Longleng Meluri Mokokchung Mon Niuland Noklak Peren Phek Shamator Tseminyü Tuensang Wokha Zünheboto Popular Sections EM Exclusive Education Editor's Pick Health News World India OPINIONS Editorial Views & Reviews Op-Ed Book Reviews Others Videos Business Science and Tech Sports Eastern Mirror About Us Contact Us Murmu embarks on 3-nation Europe tour to deepen ties with Moldova, North Macedonia, Romania President Droupadi Murmu on Sunday embarked on state visits to Moldova, North Macedonia, and Romania to deepen India's ties with the three European countries. Share NEW DELHI — President Droupadi Murmu on Sunday embarked on state visits to Moldova, North Macedonia, and Romania to deepen India's ties with the three European countries across a range of sectors, including trade and technology, and to boost people-to-people ties. The first leg of her tour begins with a visit to Moldova on Monday, marking the first-ever visit by an Indian President to the Eastern European nation. Shortly after her departure, the Rashtrapati Bhavan posted a message on X, saying, "President Droupadi Murmu embarks on state visits to the Republic of Moldova, the Republic of North Macedonia and Romania." "This is the first-ever visit by an Indian President to Moldova and North Macedonia. The visit to Romania by the President of India is taking place after a gap of over three decades," it said. Murmu will hold delegation-level talks with Moldovan President Maia Sandu and meet the President of the Parliament, Igor Grosu. She is also scheduled to interact with members of the Moldova-India Parliamentary Friendship Group, address a Business Forum, and meet with members of the Indian community. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Friday, India and Moldova enjoy warm and friendly relations and Murmu's visit would mark a significant and historical milestone and elevate bilateral ties to a broad-based partnership. "There is good scope for mutually beneficial cooperation in the areas of agriculture, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, IT and education," it said. At the invitation of the President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova, Murmu will visit North Macedonia from July 21 to 22, becoming the first Indian president to travel to the country. Popular Articles Murmu will hold bilateral talks with President Siljanovska-Davkova, meet Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski, the President of the Assembly and also address the Assembly of North Macedonia. She will also address the India-North Macedonia Business Forum. Both sides have a keen interest in deepening economic ties in priority sectors such as agriculture, pharmaceuticals, science and technology, Information Technology, and IT-enabled Services. "The visit will impart fresh momentum to India's relations with the three countries," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on X on Sunday. Also read: At least 16 killed in rain-related incidents as monsoon batters north, east India On Friday, MEA Secretary (West) Sibi George told media persons that the three-nation visit reflects India's growing engagement with central and eastern Europe. "It reaffirms our commitment to strengthening our partnerships with the countries in the region. It also complements India's broader engagement with Europe and the strategic partnership with the European Union," George had said. In the final leg of her tour, Murmu will visit Romania from July 23 to 25 at the invitation of President Nicușor Dan. It will be the first visit by an Indian president to Romania in more than three decades. Murmu will meet President Dan, interim Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, President of the Senate, Mircea Abrudean, and President of the Chamber of Deputies, Sorin Grindeanu, as well as members of the Romania-India Parliamentary Friendship Group, address the India-Romania Business Forum, and interact with members of the Indian community. The MEA said Romania is a valuable partner in the European Union, and with the conclusion of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement, the bilateral economic partnership will strengthen further in the coming years. The state visit to the three nations reflects the importance India attaches to strengthening its bilateral ties with these countries, along with New Delhi's engagement with the wider Eastern European region, it added. Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania had condemned the Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir last year and expressed their strong support to India in the fight against terrorism.

https://thegrio.com/2026/07/19/andrew-tr.text: Tristan and Andrew Tate arrested in Miami as U.K. prosecutors expand rape and trafficking charges British authorities are seeking the controversial influencers’ extradition after filing dozens of additional criminal charges involving seven alleged victims. By Bobby Pen Jul 19, 2026 Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via Email Copy Link Link Copied BUCHAREST, ROMANIA - MARCH 23: Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate talk to the media outside their residence on March 23, 2025 in Bucharest, Romania. Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan had flown to the United States last month from Romania, where they have been charged with rape, having sex with a minor, human trafficking and money laundering, charges which they deny. Their bail conditions stipulated that they had to return to Romania by March 23. (Photo by Andrei Pungovschi/Getty Images) Credit: Photo Andrei Pungovschi / Getty Images Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via Email Copy Link Link Copied Tristan and Andrew Tate arrested in Miami as U.K. prosecutors expand rape and trafficking charges British authorities are seeking the controversial influencers’ extradition after filing dozens of additional criminal charges involving seven alleged victims. Andrew Tate and his brother, Tristan Tate, were arrested by federal authorities in Miami on Saturday as British prosecutors seek to extradite the controversial social media personalities to the United Kingdom. The U.S. Marshals Service confirmed the brothers were taken into custody on July 18. Although the federal warrant reportedly remains sealed, the arrests came as the United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service announced 38 additional charges against the pair. Also Read: Advocates say Congress needs to do more to help Black and brown human trafficking victims The latest charges include allegations of rape, human trafficking, sexual assault, and bodily harm, along with offenses involving indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. The alleged crimes occurred between 2010 and 2017 and involve four additional alleged victims, according to prosecutors. Andrew Tate, 39, now faces seven new rape charges, three counts of trafficking for sexual exploitation, and three assault charges. He also faces 19 charges connected to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate, 38, faces two rape charges, one sexual assault charge, and three trafficking-related counts. Combined with charges previously authorized by British prosecutors, the brothers reportedly face 59 criminal counts involving seven alleged victims. The brothers have denied all allegations against them. Their attorney, Joseph McBride, has characterized the latest action as politically motivated and argued that British authorities violated an agreement connected to the brothers’ legal proceedings in Romania. An extradition process will determine whether they are transferred to the United Kingdom to face trial. The Tate brothers have spent years building a massive online audience around messages about masculinity, wealth and relationships. Andrew Tate, in particular, has developed an intensely loyal following among boys and young men despite widespread criticism of his statements about women. Also Read: Andrew Tate is Black? Say it ain’t so!! That influence is part of what has made the cases against the brothers larger than another celebrity legal controversy. Parents, educators and advocates have repeatedly raised concerns about young men consuming online content that presents domination, control and contempt for women as signs of strength. For Black families, the conversation is especially complicated. Black boys are already navigating racial stereotypes that often cast them as more aggressive, threatening or mature than their peers. Online personalities selling an exaggerated version of manhood can offer the appearance of confidence and control while reinforcing ideas that may leave young men emotionally isolated and women vulnerable. The brothers’ legal troubles stretch across several countries. Romanian authorities arrested Andrew and Tristan Tate in December 2022. They were later indicted on allegations including human trafficking and forming an organized criminal group, with Andrew also accused of rape. The brothers have denied wrongdoing, and the Romanian case has experienced delays and procedural complications. After Romanian officials lifted their travel restrictions, the brothers traveled to Florida in February 2025. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier subsequently announced a state criminal investigation and said prosecutors would use search warrants and subpoenas to determine whether the state had jurisdiction over any potential offenses. Saturday’s arrests, however, are tied to the British extradition effort and should not be confused with an announcement of new criminal charges filed in the United States. Andrew Tate is also expected to face a separate civil trial in the United Kingdom brought by four women who accuse him of rape, assault and coercive control. He denies those allegations as well. British prosecutors have emphasized that the Tate brothers are entitled to a fair trial and should be presumed innocent unless convicted. The arrests begin another stage of a complex international legal battle that may determine when, and where, the brothers will finally appear before a jury. https://www.thetablet.co.uk/news/vatican.text: Vatican affirms support for Ukraine with high-profile visits Patrick Hudson 19 July 2026, The Tablet Prev Next Archbishop Gallagher during a visit to the Ukrainian Catholic University in Lviv on 17 July UGCC Department of Information Archbishop Paul Gallagher’s six-day visit is his second to Ukraine, following his first shortly after the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022, while Cardinal Matteo Zuppi also visited the Lviv region and Kyiv last week. Pope Leo prayed for “countries torn apart by war and violence” after Vatican delegates visited Ukraine this week. “Let us not forget those who are suffering and dying because of these conflicts, and let us add our constant prayers to the generous efforts for peace ,” the Pope said on Sunday, speaking after the Angelus in the main square of Castel Gandolfo, outside Rome. The previous day, the Holy See’s secretary for relations with states Archbishop Paul Gallagher had visited bomb sites in Kyiv. Earlier in the week, the Archbishop of Bologna Cardinal Matteo Zuppi had made a four-day visit to Ukraine in his role as papal peace envoy. Archbishop Gallagher met parishioners at St Nicholas Church in Kyiv, which suffered a Russian missile strike in December 2024 that shattered its windows and caused severe damage to the interior. He said the community demonstrates “the virtue of perseverance”. “Perseverance is also a defining characteristic of our Catholic community. You have remained steadfast as a Eucharistic and prayerful community, and I can already see the fruits of that perseverance,” he said, emphasising Pope Leo’s support for them. “There is not a single day when he does not pray for Ukraine and for you, men and women of faith,” the archbishop continued. He voiced hope that the Pope would visit Kyiv “one day”. Gallagher later met members of the local authorities and emergency services at an apartment block destroyed by a Russian strike on 14 May which killed 24 people, including three children. Officials said that since June this year strikes have killed at least 300 people across Ukraine and injured thousands more. The archbishop also visited the St Thomas Aquinas Dominican Institute of Theology , which suffered shrapnel damage from nearby drone and missile strikes in May, and the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, the ancient monastery complex struck in a Russian attack last month . The visit officially marks 35 years since the restoration of the structures of the Latin-rite Church in Ukraine shortly before the collapse of the Soviet Union, and 25 years since the apostolic visit of John Paul II. Archbishop Gallagher arrived in the country on Thursday, travelling by road from Poland, and was received at the Krakovets border crossing by members of Ukraine’s foreign ministry. At a meeting the next day with local authorities at the curia of the Archdiocese of Lviv – the largest Roman Catholic diocese in Ukraine – Gallagher said the Church and the Pope “have not forgotten the suffering of the Ukrainian people and their sacrifices”. “A just end to the war means restoring peace to this part of Europe,” he said. “We must create the right conditions for a just peace .” On Sunday, the archbishop celebrated Mass at the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Holy Scapular in Berdychiv, alongside members of the Latin-rite hierarchy and the head of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church Major Archbishop Sviatoslav Shevchuk. “We ask the Lord God to truly heed the prayer of the Universal Catholic Church and put an end to this unjust war,” said Shevchuk in an address after the Mass. “We know that Vatican diplomacy is God’s work , because the Holy See, in particular Pope Leo XIV, is today a great herald of authentic peace.” The six-day visit is Gallagher’s second to Ukraine, following his first shortly after the full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022. Earlier this week, Cardinal Zuppi also visited the Lviv region and Kyiv. He previously travelled to the country in June 2023, when Pope Francis appointed him as his peace envoy, and has since worked to facilitate prisoner exchanges . After his arrival on Monday, Zuppi met prisoners of war held in the Zakhid-1 detention centre near Lviv and told them Pope Leo “is praying for you, that the war may end and that you may return home”. The prisoners, captured by Ukrainian forces while fighting with the Russian army, come from more than 50 countries. The cardinal distributed gifts sent by Pope Leo to the prisoners, including prayer cards and keychains. “The Pope asked me to bring you a keychain. I hope that soon you’ll put your house key on it,” he said. “We want to tell you today to look to the future with hope – that you will return home, that the war will end. And we pray fervently that it will end soon.” On Wednesday, Cardinal Zuppi offered a prayer during a ceremony in Kyiv for Ukrainian Statehood Day, marked on the same day as the commemoration of the Baptism of Kyivan Rus’ by Prince Volodymyr the Great in 988. “Grant a just peace. May prisoners return home, may children embrace their families once again, may the missing be found, and may everyone be able to mourn over the body of their loved one who has fallen. Inspire in each one of us the courage and wisdom to become builders of peace,” Zuppi said. During the ceremony in St Michael’s Square, the cardinal took part in a wreath-laying ceremony alongside President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, placing a bouquet of red roses before the Wall of Remembrance commemorating those killed in the war with Russia. Ukraine’s Ambassador to the Holy See Andrii Yurash called this an “exceptional gesture of respect toward Ukraine, acknowledging its statehood tradition, which dates back more than 1,000 years, as well as its ongoing struggle for independence in the war against the Russian aggressor”. Later that day, Zuppi met Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha for further discussion of prisoner exchanges and the repatriation of detained civilians and children. According to Vatican News, Ukrainian officials also requested the Holy See’s support for an “all-for-all” exchange involving around 7,000 Ukrainian prisoners held in Russia and roughly 4,000 Russian prisoners in Ukraine. “Even one soldier, one civilian or one child reunited with their family is a step towards peace,” Zuppi said. “Every possible effort will be made. This is the will of Leo XIV. Humanitarian commitment must stand above political or military considerations.” Archbishop gives Pope Leo list of Ukrainian prisoners Joy amid sorrow: two weeks in Ukraine Stay updated — add us as a preferred news source on Google: Archbishop Paul Gallagher Cardinal Matteo Zuppi CATHOLIC NEWS peace Pope Leo XIV prisoners of war Russia Russian invasion of Ukraine Ukraine Vatican diplomacy Help us keep The Tablet’s voice independent, clear and far-reaching. Read more A t 6:29am on 7 October 2023, Mia Schem was filming a video with her friend Elia Toledano when the sound of rockets started. They had been waiting for the sun to rise over the Negev desert in southern Israel at the Nova music festival, just 3 miles from the Israel- Gaza border. By the end of the day, the 21-year-old describes how she was shot in the arm by a Hamas militant and taken hostage into the Gaza Strip, and 378 people from the festival would be among 1,200 people killed. Israel launched a relentless two-year barrage of strikes in response, leaving 70,000 Palestinians dead in Gaza and reducing much of the enclave to rubble. In the early days of the war, Hamas released a video of Schem in captivity , the first footage of any of the 251 hostages. The French- Israeli citizen was held in Gaza for 55 days before being released during a brief truce between Israel and Hamas. open image in gallery Mia Schem, 21, appears in a Hamas hostage video in the days following the 7 October attacks. ( AFP/Hamas handout ) Speaking with The Independent in London, Schem has flown from her home in Shoham, a town on the outskirts of Tel Aviv in Israel. She said she had only decided to attend the music festival on a whim. “I remember that I asked Elia, ‘Do you want to go to the Nova Festival?’ and he tell me ‘Yes, why not?’” she says. She drove to Toledano’s house, her best friend, and they took his car to the festival site. “I didn’t know the party was close to Gaza,” she says, because the organisers of the Nova festival tended to share the locations of the raves only a few hours before the scheduled start time. Even if she had known that information, it would not have impacted her decision to go. “Who thought that something like that would happen,” she says. open image in gallery Palestinian militants move towards the border fence with Israel from Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip on October 7, 2023. ( AFP via Getty Images ) Once the rockets started, Schem grabbed Toledano and headed straight for his car. She believes they were one of the first few cars to leave the Nova festival site. At this stage in the day seemingly innocuous decisions would decide whether or not you would survive the terrorist attack. When leaving the festival site those who turned right were saved, Schem says, and those who turned left towards Tel Aviv and Jerusalem were met by Hamas. “Me and Elia were the first people to see the terrorists,” she says. Hamas gunmen were standing at either side of the road, shooting at cars and killing passengers as they sped past. Schem thought there could have been as many as 40 gunmen in the road. Schem floored it through the roadblock but says their car was riddled with bullets. open image in gallery Abandoned vehicles at the site of the 7 October attack on the Nova music festival in the Negev desert in southern Israel. ( AFP via Getty Images ) The vehicle rolled twice, and Toledano and Schem were forced to escape out of the vehicle’s windows, as the doors were jammed. They tried to hide next to the car. Toledano grabbed her phone and began calling the emergency services, but the messages that came back were grim. “They tell us on the phone, ‘You need to hide. We can’t help you,’” Schem says, “Nobody came to save us.” When she was hiding on the ground, she was shot in the arm by a Hamas terrorist: “ They shot me from point-blank range.” Both Schem and Toledano were abducted and taken into Gaza. Only one of them would return alive. The body of Elia Toledano would be eventually retrieved by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) from the Gaza Strip in late 2023. There was a “ high probability ” that his cause of death was due to an Israeli airstrike, according to an IDF investigation. open image in gallery Palestinian militants transport a reportedly captured Israeli woman by motorcycle, in Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip. ( AFP via Getty Images ) When describing her time in Hamas captivity in Gaza, Schem is unequivocal. She was treated like an “animal in a cage,” she recounts. She believes the only reason she was saved from being raped was because she was being kept in the home of her captor. “He didn’t touch me, but the reason was because his wife and children were behind the door,” Schem adds. She said her captor’s wife would mistreat Schem because she resented the fact that she was in the same room as her husband: “She didn’t give me water or food.” Five days before she was released, Schem says she was taken down into the tunnels beneath Gaza where she first encountered other hostages.Five women were also being held there. Schem has told Israeli television that this was the hardest time of her captivity because of the hopelessness of the hostages she met down there. open image in gallery Visitors walk among burnt out cars and tents at the Nova Music Festival Exhibition in Berlin, Germany. ( Getty Images ) Schem was in London to recount her story to an audience at the Nova Exhibition. The exhibition recreates the music festival with real wreckage brought over from Israel. “ It's a miracle that I'm here.” she says, “and if God saved me, I never give up.” The exhibition has been travelling around the world, and London is the 10th city it has visited so far. Now, plans are underway for the exhibition to travel to Paris, Budapest and Prague in the future. When the exhibition travelled to New York, hundreds of people gathered in Lower Manhattan to protest against Israel’s conduct since October 7th, with some accusing the show of being political propaganda. In his Facebook post, Magyar described Polgar as a figure "synonymous with talent and perseverance," adding that the country needs "unity, peace, and a president of whom every Hungarian can be proud." He said the presidency represents "the highest form of service," and that he would consider it an honor if Polgar accepted the nomination. Polgar, born in Budapest in 1976, is a Hungarian chess grandmaster and a five-time Chess Olympiad champion. Hungarian President Tamas Sulyok on Saturday signed the country's 17th constitutional amendment, triggering the end of his mandate as head of state. https://www.mirror.co.uk/travel/news/fli.text: A teacher hopped on a plane to France for lunch and claims it was more affordable than a standard day out in the UK. Claire Howard jetted off to Beauvais, France , for a leisurely day of dining, exploring and sunshine and was back home before midnight. The 48-year-old woman found return Ryanair flights for merely £27 and secured them a month beforehand. The early morning flight departed Birmingham at approximately 7.30am, with the homebound journey leaving at 11pm. Her husband gave her a lift to the airport, and she caught a £1.80 bus to Beauvais that took 15 minutes. Claire, who is a mum, believes the entire trip, including flights, buses, food, and drink, came to roughly £70. Claire, from Birmingham, said: "I've been to Paris a few times and didn't want to travel in from Beauvais as Paris is really pricey and busy. "I just wanted to see what was actually in Beauvais itself for a relaxing day of wandering, eating, and drinking. I just saw on Skyscanner that return flights were only £27, so I went for it. "It's exciting to go to a different country just for lunch or to explore for a day. The bus from the airport to the centre is very cheap. It's just a different feeling abroad. "It makes it feel much more like an adventure than just going somewhere at home. I don't want to pay £50 to go to the cinema and lunch here in a shopping centre when I can go and experience so much more abroad for a very reasonable price." The English teacher spent her morning exploring the city's weekly Saturday market, treating herself to a coffee and a pain au chocolat for just £4. She then unwound with a drink in the town square, soaking up live music before hopping in a £10 Uber to Plan d'Eau du Canada, a beloved lakeside destination. For lunch, she put together an £8 French-style picnic featuring a supermarket baguette, cheese, and a small bottle of wine, which she enjoyed while reading and sunbathing beside the water. Her packed itinerary also took in Beauvais Cathedral and the neighbouring Musée de l'Oise, both of which were completely free to enter. The day wrapped up with a Pad Thai supper at a nearby Thai restaurant for roughly £10, before she made her way back to the airport for her evening flight home. She also picked up an £8 bracelet as a memento of her trip. Claire said: "I'd say it could probably be done even cheaper. I do stay over in some places depending on flight times but it wasn't necessary for this trip as the flight times fit and I could still have an evening meal and a full day. "There's no point in staying over to get a flight home the next morning as it's a waste of accommodation money." Claire admits she's become completely addicted to budget day trips overseas after stumbling across bargain flights from Birmingham Airport, jetting off to a new destination almost every month. Just this year alone, she's already ticked off Bergamo in Italy, Malaga in Spain, Valetta in Malta, Poznan in Poland, and Porto in Portugal. She's already snapped up return flights to Poland and Berlin in August for just £70. Claire said: "I'm just led by what is possible and affordable. I can't take time off at all in term time but I have Tuesdays off so I do like to make use of them. "I just love the way you can do and see so much in the same time that you might waste a day at home just watching Netflix and doomscrolling. I usually find the best prices four to six weeks in advance. My husband doesn't like short trips so he's not jealous."

(Photo By: DNG News / YouTube / MGN) LONDON (AP) — Influencer brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested Saturday in Miami after U.K. prosecutors said they brought further rape and sex trafficking charges against them. Britain’s Crown Prosecution Service said the new charges relate to four further victims and were brought after authorities received evidence from Bedfordshire Police in southeastern England. The charges include rape, assault, trafficking and offenses relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.” The charges announced Saturday, which bring the total number of alleged victims in the U.K. to seven, are the latest in a long-running international legal saga involving the brothers that has spanned the U.S., Britain and Romania. The brothers have denied wrongdoing. An attorney for the brothers, Joseph McBride, blasted the latest charges as “filth and slander.” In a phone interview Sunday, he said he was confident the extradition request would ultimately be denied. Here are some things to know about the Tate brothers: Who the Tate Brothers are Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, are dual U.S.-British citizens known for their social media empire promoting wealth, male dominance and misogyny. Andrew Tate is a former professional kickboxer and self-described misogynist who has amassed more than 10 million followers, most of them boys and young men, on X. He has been banned from platforms like YouTube, TikTok and Instagram for violating hate speech guidelines. He also runs an online academy where he says he teaches young men how to get rich and attract women. Tristan Tate is also a former kickboxer. The brothers are avid supporters of U.S. President Donald Trump. What the Tates are charged with Andrew Tate and his brother have faced multiple charges in the U.K. and Romania, where they moved to in 2016. British prosecutors said the new charges relate to alleged offenses that took place between 2010 and 2017. They said Andrew Tate was charged with seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault and 19 charges for offenses relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate was charged with one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating sex trafficking. The Crown Prosecution Service said in a statement it “has requested the extradition of the Tates from the U.S. They have been arrested and await extradition proceedings to the U.K.” The Tates already face previous charges of rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other alleged victims in the U.K. between 2012 and 2015. In June, a U.K. High Court judge threw out a legal bid by the Tates to be told the names of their accusers. In Romania, the siblings were arrested in late 2022 along with two Romanian women. The four were accused of participating in criminal schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations and the Romanian case hasn’t gone forward because of legal and procedural problems. The case hasn’t been closed, and there is also a separate legal case against the brothers in Romania. Andrew Tate has repeatedly claimed that prosecutors in Romania have no evidence against him and that there is a political conspiracy to silence him. How the extradition process could work The brothers are expected to appear Monday before a magistrate judge in Miami, where they are currently being held in federal detention. Bail is rarely granted to those held for international extradition, and their lawyer said he expects they will remain jailed for the time being. In the coming weeks, a U.S. district judge will consider whether they meet the conditions for extradition. The ultimate decision about whether to order the extradition will fall to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. While the State Department has some discretion to deny extradition requests from the U.K., it has granted nearly every British request since ratifying a strengthened extradition treaty in 2007. One exception came during Trump’s first term, when the U.S. declined an extradition request for the wife of a former American diplomat involved in a fatal crash in England, citing diplomatic immunity. The rejection prompted an international outcry. Why the Tates were in the U.S. British police previously sought the Tates’ extradition to the U.K. once their legal proceedings in Romania concluded. But in February 2025 they were allowed to leave Romania after authorities lifted travel restrictions, and they flew to Florida on a private jet. Romania’s foreign minister said at the time that a U.S. official in the Trump administration had expressed interest in the brothers’ legal case in Romania. Trump said he knew “nothing about” the case when asked if his administration pressured the Romania government to release the Tates. Andrew Tate By CNN Newssource July 19, 2026 5:56 PM Published July 19, 2026 4:19 PM By Holmes Lybrand, Dalia Faheid, Hannah Rabinowitz, Alea Motwane, CNN (CNN) — US Marshals arrested social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate in Miami Saturday on an extradition request from the United Kingdom following an investigation into sexual offenses reported by seven victims, according to the UK Crown Prosecution Service. UK officials accused the brothers of abusing women in the East of England region, just north of London, between 2010 and 2017. Andrew Tate, a self-proclaimed misogynist with billions of views online, faces 42 charges, including rape, human trafficking, indecent images of a child and assault, according to the UK Crown Prosecution Service and Bedfordshire Police . Tristan Tate faces 17 charges, including sexual assault, rape and trafficking, officials said. “Officers from our major crime unit have been working closely alongside the Crown Prosecution Service and both national and international law enforcement agencies as part of this complex investigation,” Bedfordshire Assistant Chief Constable Karena Thomas said. The Department of Justice confirmed US Marshals arrested Andrew and Tristan Tate “pursuant to extradition proceedings,” adding the arrests “were made in accordance with the treaties and law enforcement agreements governing Justice Department extraditions.” The brothers will appear in Miami federal court on Monday, their attorney, Joeseph McBride, told CNN on Sunday. The brothers are expected to reject the extradition request, McBride added. The brothers are innocent, McBride said and criticized the UK’s move to seek extradition. “There is a long-standing agreement between the UK and Romanian governments that the UK would not seek extradition while the Romanian proceedings are pending,” McBride said. “Those proceedings are ongoing right now. That agreement exists because no nation gets to trample the judicial sovereignty of another for political convenience.” In a statement posted to X Sunday, McBride said the brothers were arrested for their politics and are being held in solitary confinement. The brothers were in Washington, DC, earlier this month where they held political meetings, McBride told CNN. CNN has reached out to Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier for information about where and how the brothers are being held. Romanian prosecutors previously accused the brothers of trafficking women across Romania, the United Kingdom and the US and sexually exploiting them. The Tates have repeatedly rejected the allegations made against them in that case. CNN has reached out to Romania’s justice ministry for comment on their arrest. Advocates have warned against the pair’s rising tide of influence among young boys and men. Andrew Tate is known for his aggressive speech about male dominance, female submission and wealth. At one point, he was suspended from major social media platforms. The brothers, who have dual American and British citizenship, face dozens of new charges added onto previous charges brought by the Crown Prosecution Service after evidence was submitted by Bedfordshire Police, authorities said. The new charges were brought after officials had investigated reports made by four additional victims in the East England areas of Bedfordshire and Hertfordshire, police said. Andrew Tate is also facing a civil suit in the UK, which is being brought by four women who accuse the social media influencer of rape. A spokesperson for Tate previously told CNN that their client “categorically denies these unproven and untested allegations.” Matthew Jury, an attorney representing the four women, welcomed Tate’s arrest. “We do not yet know whether these new charges relate to the complaints made by my clients or by other women,” Jury said in a statement Sunday. “But any step that advances the proper administration of justice deserves to be welcomed.” The brothers left Romania after Romanian authorities lifted travel restrictions on them, arriving in Florida in February 2025. Upon their arrival, they found themselves at the heart of another criminal investigation — when Attorney General Uthmeier announced the probe, led by the Office of Statewide Prosecution. They had taken aim at Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, who previously suggested they were not welcome in his state. “When Americans who are unfairly imprisoned abroad return home you betray them,” Andrew Tate said on X last year. “You better nail me now. Let’s go. Arrest me.” Thomas, the Bedfordshire Police official, said “there is no place for male violence against women and girls.” “We will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,” Thomas said. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images Spain Chaos of border crossing gives way to limbo for Moroccans on Ceuta’s streets People among the more than 50,000 who entered Spanish enclave this week describe the journey and their prospects Okba Mohammad and Javier Jennings Mozo in Ceuta Sun 2 Aug 2026 09.11 EDT Last modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 13.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google F our days ago, Youssef El Abbas saw an opportunity to reclaim the life he had lost seven years earlier. News was circulating that about 400 people had swum from Morocco to the neighbouring Spanish enclave of Ceuta on the north African coast, approximately 12 miles (19km) across the strait of Gibraltar from mainland Spain. Here was a chance for the 44-year-old Moroccan father of four to return to Spain , from which he had been deported when his residency expired after the loss of his job in Bilbao in 2019. El Abbas took a taxi and headed to the city of Tétouan, south of the enclave. While en route, he saw Facebook posts and news reports claiming that the Moroccan authorities were allowing people to pass through their side of the border. That meant that unlike those who had crossed the previous night, he could simply travel overland before swimming for just five minutes across the border from Moroccan to Spanish territory to avoid the Spanish border controls. View image in fullscreen People returning to Morocco on Sunday after crossing into Ceuta. Photograph: Reduan Dris/EPA He reached Tétouan to find the city completely overwhelmed. “Young men were running through the streets, flooding every corner,” he said. By the time a second taxi took El Abbas to Fnideq, the town bordering Ceuta, he realised that the usual blockades and checkpoints preventing people without European documents from even approaching the frontier had been removed. View image in fullscreen Youssef El Abbas in Ceuta. Photograph: Okba Mohammad “The Moroccan police were shouting at us: ‘Go, go, go! Run now, run into Spain,’” he said. “The night before, they were beating people. But that morning they were letting us through. Nothing made sense.” Despite the crowds, El Abbas noticed the police were only letting Moroccans cross over. “All the sub-Saharan migrants were being pushed back by force.” He reached the border at 2.45pm on Wednesday. By 3pm, after a short swim, he was standing on Spanish soil. Not everyone was so lucky. “In just 10 minutes in the water, I saw four people floating dead in Moroccan waters,” he said. “People were pulling their bodies out.” They were among at least 72 people who drowned or were crushed trying to reach the Spanish territory. El Abbas is just one of the 50,000 or so people to have crossed into Ceuta this week , in what Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, described as “a violation of Spain’s territorial integrity”. Map showing location of Ceuta between Morocco and Spain, and another map showing line of Morocco-Ceuta border and Tarajal breakwater Madrid has attributed the latest influx to “human-trafficking mafias” that have taken advantage of a decision by Spain’s supreme court, which recently ruled that those intercepted at sea while trying to enter Ceuta or Melilla – the other Spanish enclave on the north African coast – could not be summarily returned under special rules. The same hand that helped me out of the water was the one that later hit me But there has also been speculation that the Moroccan authorities may have opened the border to signal their displeasure at Sánchez’s recent visit to Algeria, which supports efforts to free the disputed territory of Western Sahara from Moroccan occupation. Morocco’s ambassador to Spain, Karima Benyaich Millán, said Rabat was not happy about the mass crossing, adding that it hoped those in Ceuta would return. Moroccan government sources told the Europa Press news agency that the surge of people entering Ceuta was down to “criminal organisations” and insisted that Rabat’s cooperation with Spain remained “exemplary”. In May 2021, Rabat loosened border controls – allowing 10,000 people to cross into Ceuta over the course of two days – during a diplomatic standoff triggered after Madrid allowed a Western Sahara independence leader to be treated for Covid-19 in Spain. View image in fullscreen A man bends down to pick up a pair of shoes from debris washed up on Ceuta’s shore. Photograph: Pedro Nunes/Reuters El Abbas said he had never stopped dreaming of returning to Spain, where he had worked mainly in the hospitality sector for 14 years. Since being deported to Morocco in 2019, he has lived apart from his wife and four daughters, who remain in the northern Spanish city of Bilbao, while scraping by with occasional work repairing mobile phones alongside his father. “I never stopped thinking about coming back,” he said. “In Morocco, I was alive, but I wasn’t really living.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day Preview latest after newsletter promotion Why is Ceuta a migration flashpoint and how were so many people able to cross from Morocco? Read more The return has been bittersweet. When he swam ashore in Ceuta, a Spanish Guardia Civil officer extended a hand to pull him from the sea. But that gesture of aid eventually gave way to one of violence. Three days after arriving, the group of people he was with were surrounded by a military patrol and beaten. “The same hand that helped me out of the water was the one that later hit me,” he said. El Abbas’s story is hardly unique. Although more than 48,000 people had crossed back into Morocco by Friday night, hundreds are still sleeping in parks, public squares and on pavements, waiting for a chance to move on or simply to find somewhere to rest. It appears to be virtually impossible for migrants to leave Ceuta for mainland Spain. Said, 17, from Casablanca, was sitting on a kerb a few hundred metres away. He, too, had joined the Ceuta-bound crowds when he heard that the border was open. But the jubilation had given way to reality and all he had was a bottle of water and the carton of yoghurt a local resident had given him. 3:37 Tens of thousands of migrants cross into Spanish enclave Ceuta from Morocco - video The teenager said he was taken to a centre for unaccompanied minors after he crossed, but there were no places available, so he ended up back on the streets. According to a soldier who asked to remain anonymous, the current protocol for the authorities – including the military, the police and the Guardia Civil – is to treat unaccompanied minors as regular migrants and return them to Morocco. Said and the other teenagers with him said no one would sell them food or allow them into shops and restaurants because they did not speak Spanish. Three days after the mass influx, Ceuta is slowly trying to recover a sense of normality. By early evening on Saturday, cafe terraces were beginning to fill again and some businesses had reopened their doors. Many of the remaining arrivals are being tended to by Ceuta locals, who walk the streets handing out bottles of water, sandwiches, blankets and clothes. Others stop to ask if they need help or to offer to call a relative. Such shows of solidarity have been threatened by the arrival of far-right politicians and a neo-Nazi group, all keen to use the humanitarian crisis for their own ends. “They’re going to exploit our feelings to claim the credit and say they defended Ceuta,” said a local woman called Malika. “We don’t want them here. If they want to defend something, they should go somewhere else.” View image in fullscreen People who crossed into Ceuta this week are escorted back to Morocco by the Spanish army on Saturday. Photograph: Antonio Sempere/AP Malika, who was born in Ceuta to a soldier who served in the Spanish army, rejected the notion that the city should be defined solely by the political confrontation that followed this week’s mass arrival. But she also acknowledged the pressure on a city of just over 80,000 people. “It would have been an impossible situation for any city,” she said. Fatima Hamed Hossain, a member of Ceuta’s assembly, fears that the strain created by the crisis has deepened divisions within the city. “Everything we’ve lived through has created tensions between neighbours,” she said. “That’s exactly what feeds the far right.” As a caravan of people returned back over the border, Said’s mind was on the future. His goal is simple: get a place in a protection centre, spend the next year learning Spanish and, once he turns 18, find work as a barber. What he fears most is ending up without legal documentation and seeing that plan collapse before it has even begun. Leaving is not on his agenda, however. “All I need,” he said, “is a chance.” Explore more on these topics Spain Morocco Migration Africa Europe Middle East and north Africa news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/a.text: Former radio broadcaster Alan Jones faces 22 charges of sexual assault between 2003 and 2020. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP View image in fullscreen Former radio broadcaster Alan Jones faces 22 charges of sexual assault between 2003 and 2020. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP Alan Jones Alan Jones trial on indecent assault and sexual touching charges begins in Sydney The 85-year-old former broadcaster faces 22 charges from six different complainants in what is expected to be a four-month trial Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Amanda Meade and Jordyn Beazley Sun 2 Aug 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Sun 2 Aug 2026 11.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The high-profile trial of former broadcaster Alan Jones for indecent assault and sexual touching charges begins on Monday in Sydney’s Downing Centre local court and is expected to run for four months and hear from 76 witnesses. Judge Glenn Walsh will hear from six complainants who were allegedly indecently assaulted by the 85-year-old between 2003 and 2020. Jones is facing 22 charges at his judge-alone trial. They include 20 indecent assault and two sexual touching charges, the court was told in pre-trial hearings last month. In 2018 the offence of indecent assault was replaced by sexual touching, carrying a maximum penalty of five years imprisonment. The youngest complainant, who was 17 at the time of the alleged offending, is giving evidence in camera – presented in a closed courtroom – on Monday after the delivery of opening statements by the prosecution and the defence. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email On Friday, Walsh knocked back an attempt by the defence to prevent media reporting the evidence of complainants. Jones’s barrister Claire O’Neill argued that under the criminal procedure act, in-camera evidence was not permitted to be published. But Walsh did not agree, saying he wasn’t satisfied in-camera meant “a non-publication or suppression order”. He also said Complainant J was not “fussed” by media reporting his evidence. “The Complainant J doesn’t seem to be jumping up for the crown to say no, but the defendant is.” Complainant J is anonymised in line with the right of all alleged victims of sexual offences to maintain their privacy. The court heard in pre-trial arguments Complainant J, whose case accounts for nine of the 22 charges, told police he met Jones as a young man and was given a mobile phone by the then 2GB breakfast host, who invited him to visit his Macquarie Street apartment. Jones is alleged to have put his arms around Complainant J at the apartment, and give him a “squeeze” and a “peck” on the mouth while saying “I love you mate”. The court has heard that Jones allegedly touched Complainant J’s penis while he was driving him to Fitzroy Falls in the NSW southern highlands. The prosecution case is that there is a pattern of alleged behaviour by Jones involving the targeting of “significantly younger men” in his professional and social circle. Prosecutors told the court last month in pre-trial that it is “improbable” that two similar accounts of Jones allegedly touching a complainant’s penis while driving would be “untrue”. Each complainant was driving a car and there was “no reciprocity prior to the touching”, the court heard. Two of the six complainants told police they were assaulted on the first occasion they met Jones: one at a fashion show and one at a fundraising meeting. Jones has denied all wrongdoing and said the allegations are all either baseless or they distort the truth. “I have never indecently assaulted these people,” he said outside court in December 2024. “The law assumes that I am not guilty, and I am not guilty.” NSW police formed Taskforce Bonnefin after alleged victims came forward in the wake of a report in the Sydney Morning Herald and the Age.
