https://telex.hu/transtelex/2026/08/06/c.text: Menü Kereső Nem először áll le a csernavodai erőmű szárazság miatt, de azóta kiszolgáltatottabb lett Románia energiarendszere Transtelex Legfontosabb A csernavodai atomerőmű 2026. augusztus 4-én – Fotó: Alex Nicodim / Anadolu / AFP Zsizsmann Erika (Transtelex) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A Duna alacsony hozama miatt az 1-es reaktort július 28-án leállították. Az erőmű Románia energiafogyasztásának 20 százalékát biztosítja. Nem először állt le a csernavodai atomerőmű a Duna alacsony vízszintje miatt, a romániai hatóságok mégis sürgősségi üzemmódban végezték el a munkálatokat, amelyekről évtizedek óta tudják, hogy szükségesek. Az ország villamosenergia-deficitjéhez ugyanakkor a nukleáris energia kiesésénél jóval nagyobb mértékben járul hozzá a vízenergia megcsappanása és az energiatároló-kapacitás szűkössége. A nemzetközi sajtóba is eljutott a hír , hogy a román haditengerészet egy Duna-parti szikla felrobbantásával , mederkotrással és kővel megrakott uszályok elsüllyesztésével próbálja megvédeni utolsó működő atomreaktorát a leállástól. Az Ostrovi-ág (Öreg-Duna) vízhozamának növelését célzó akció nem most jutott a hatóságok eszébe, a szikla felrobbantásával már 1953-ban is próbálkoztak , 2003-ban pedig, amikor szintén a Duna alacsony vízszintje miatt állt le az akkori egyetlen blokk, ismét felmerült. 2003. augusztus 23-án Baziaşnál 1640 m³/s volt a Duna hozama (most ennél kisebb, szerdán már elérte az 1400 m³/s-os, valaha mért legalacsonyabb szintet ), az atomerőmű pedig elegendő hűtővíz hiányában leállt. Csak több mint három hét múlva, szeptember 16-án indították újra. Akkor is az 1-es blokk vált működésképtelenné, amit most is elsőként állítottak le , a 2-es reaktor pedig akkor még nem működött, azt csak 2007-ben üzemelték be. A csernavodai atomerőmű akkor az ország energiafogyasztásának mintegy 10 százalékát biztosította, a leállás pedig az akkori árfolyamon 7,2 millió eurós veszteséget jelentett üzemeltetőjének, az akkor még teljes egészében állami tulajdonban lévő Nuclearelectricának. Az Ostrovi-ág vízhozamának növelését már akkor szükséges intézkedésként emlegették , a dobrudzsai vízügyi igazgatóság pedig a Ziua de Constanța szerint 2004-ben javasolta a Duna szabályozását a Bala-ág és az Ostrovi-ág elágazásánál, hogy hosszú távon biztosítsák a hajózáshoz és az atomerőmű működtetéséhez szükséges feltételeket. Bár bizonyos munkálatokat a 2010-es évek elején elvégeztek, az átfogóbb projekt műszaki-gazdasági mutatóit csak 2024-ben hagyta jóvá a kormány, miután többször nekifutottak a terveknek, és sikerült úgy alakítani őket, hogy a tőkehalak vándorlási útvonalát se veszélyeztessék. A beruházást azonban azóta se valósították meg, nem került pénz rá . Ilie Bolojan ügyvivő miniszterelnök múlt héten, az 1-es reaktor leállása miatt már prioritásként emlegette . Romániát 23 év után energetikai szempontból ismét felkészületlenül érte a Duna vízszintjének drasztikus csökkenése. Nem sokkal azután, hogy az 1-es blokkot leválasztották az országos energetikai rendszerről, a Nuclearelectrica közölte , hogy a 2-es reaktort legkésőbb másnap reggel szintén leállítják. Július 30-i, csütörtök déli újabb közleményében a vállalat viszont arról tájékoztatott, hogy a 2-es reaktor egyelőre mégis tovább üzemel. Ezt hivatalosan azzal indokolták, hogy az atomerőmű szakemberei az éjszaka folyamán megállapították, hogy a reaktor biztonságos körülmények között működtethető, az ehhez szükséges paraméterek stabilak voltak. Hozzátették ugyanakkor, hogy a leállás bármikor szükségessé válhat. A hirtelen fordulatot Dumitru Chisăliță, az Intelligens Energia Egyesület elnöke úgy értelmezte , hogy a hatóságok belátták, a kánikula miatt várható magas fogyasztás és a korlátozott importlehetőségek miatt a 2-es reaktor üzemeltetésének folytatása a kevésbé kockázatos választás, és inkább nekiláttak a sürgősségi beavatkozásnak. Ennek egyelőre a hivatalos álláspont szerint az volt az eredménye, hogy kedd reggelre két centimétert emelkedett a Duna vízszintje az erőműnél, és a 2-es reaktor várhatóan két nappal hosszabb ideig működhet . Fontos különbség a 2026-os és a 2003-as leállás között, hogy két évtizeddel ezelőtt még másként nézett ki Románia energiaellátása. Az ország akkor nettó villamosenergia-exportőr volt, még úgy is, hogy a csernavodai erőmű 1-es reaktorának kiesése és a vízerőművek gyengébb termelése miatt leállították az exportot. 2003-ban Románia 1 terawattóra (TWh, azaz egymillió megawattóra) áramot importált és 3 terawattórát exportált a Transtelectrica éves jelentése szerint . A tendencia azóta megfordult, 2025-ben például 18,256 TWh-t importált és csak 14,513 TWh-t exportált az ország az Országos Statisztikai Intézet (INS) adatai szerint . A legnagyobb változást a széntüzelésű erőművek fokozatos bezárása hozta. Az Országos Energetikai Szabályozó Hatóság (ANRE) jelentése szerint 2003-ban a legnagyobb mértékben, 41 százalékban a szénerőműveket használták energiatermelésre, ezzel szemben ma a teljes beépített teljesítmény 9,8 százalékát (1,9 GW) teszik ki. A beépített teljesítményt energiaforrások szerinti bontásban ezen az oldalon lehet megnézni . A környezetszennyező lignit- és feketeszénalapú erőművek, valamint az azokat ellátó bányák fokozatos bezárása Románia vállalása az Európai Unió felé, ez az országos helyreállítási terv keretében kapott uniós támogatás egyik feltétele. A pótlásukat szolgáló fejlesztések akadozása miatt ugyanakkor Románia energiabiztonsága és importfüggősége nőtt. Bár az Európai Bizottság korábban beleegyezett az erőműbezárások részleges elhalasztásába, a szén körül továbbra is nagy a politikai feszültség. A Szociáldemokrata Párt (PSD) és a Románok Egyesüléséért Szövetség (AUR) kihasználta a válsághelyzetet a dekarbonizációs határidőt érintő módosító javaslat megszavazására , aminek viszont a liberális tábor szerint súlyos következményei lehetnek Románia uniós pénzeit illetően. Kölcsönösen vádolják a politikai pártok egymást azzal is, hogy miért nem készültek el időben az alternatív energiatermelő kapacitások. A csernavodai 1-es blokk beépített teljesítménye 706,5 MW, a 2-es blokké 704,8 MW, így a két blokk egyidejű kiesése több mint 1400 MW termelőkapacitás elvesztését jelentheti az országos hálózat számára, ekkor Romániának a villamosenergia-fogyasztás közel 20 százalékát kellene más forrásból pótolnia. A Transelectrica adatai szerint az esti órákban Romániának rendszeresen 2000 MW feletti villamosenergia-deficitje van, amit egyre drágább importból fedez. A deficithez viszont a csernavodai 1-es reaktor leállásánál nagyobb mértékben járul hozzá az, hogy a szárazság miatt a vízerőművek termelése is jelentősen visszaesett. A vízerőművek 6,68 GW beépített teljesítménye a romániai energetikai rendszer legjelentősebb komponense, de most nem lép 1,2-1,5 GW fölé, a Vaskapu 1 és 2 teljesítménye a negyedére csökkent . „Az olcsó és rugalmas vízenergia éveken át megmentette az energetikai rendszerünket és megmentett a magas számláktól is. Ma viszont egyszerűen nincs ehhez elég víz” – jegyezte meg Facebookon közzétett elemzésében Corina Murafa energetikai szakértő, az Európai Gazdasági és Szociális Bizottság tagja. Murafa azt az álláspontot képviseli, hogy a klímaváltozásnak kitett vízerőművet, atomreaktort építeni vagy a fosszilis tüzelőanyagokra alapozni nem vezet előre, ehelyett megújuló energiába és a tárolókapacitásba kellene fektetni és dinamikus díjazással az olcsóbb termelési időszakok felé kellene terelni a fogyasztókat. A szakértő „fantáziaprojekteknek” nevezte a vízerőművek építését vagy befejezését, ezzel arra a kilenc közérdekűnek nyilvánított vízerőműre utalva, amelyért a romániai politikai elit zöme még a természetvédelmi területeket is beáldozná egy nemrég megszavazott törvény szerint. 2003 óta Romániában kiépült a szél- és napenergia-termelés, ma már ezeknek az eszközöknek összesen 6,47 GW a beépített teljesítménye, ami a teljes termelési kapacitás 33,34 százalékát teszi ki. A működésük azonban időjárás- és napszakfüggő, az esti csúcsidőszakban például a napenergia eleve kiesik a termelésből, így este hét és tíz között a fogyasztás rendszeresen több mint 2000 MW-tal haladja meg a termelést. A probléma az, hogy a napközben megtermelt olcsó áram nagy részét exportálja Románia, este pedig, amikor a nagy kereslet miatt a legdrágább az áram, importra szorul. Hiába fedezi a napenergia délben a fogyasztás 70 százalékát, ha naplemente után a rendszer víz- és gázerőművekre, importra, illetve a szűkös tárolókapacitásokra alapoz, amelyek magas költsége közvetlenül beépül az esti csúcsidőszak áraiba, figyelmeztetett még júniusban Dumitru Chisăliță, az Intelligens Energia Egyesület (AEI) elnöke. A különbség nagy, Sebastian Burduja liberális képviselő, volt energiügyi miniszter szerint áprilisban Románia 33 millió eurót fizetett az importált áramért, miközben csak 5 millió eurót kapott az exportért. Bulgária például Romániánál sokkal többet fordított az országos helyreállítási terv keretében tárolókapacitásra, az akkumulátorai már most elérik az 1181 MW beépített teljesítményt és a 2,5 GWh energiatároló kapacitást, a következő években pedig közel 14 GWh tárolókapacitást üzemelnének be. Románia is igyekszik , az utóbbi hónapokban elérte a 989 MW beépített teljesítményt és az 1 975 MWh energiatároló kapacitást. Még 2025 decemberében adták át az ország eddigi legnagyobb akkumulátortelepét a Kolozsvár melletti Szászfenesen, az elmúlt hónapokban pedig a Bánságban és a Bărăganon is új energiatárolókat kapcsoltak a rendszerre. Az ország egyébként idén nem először nélkülözi a csernavodai atomerőmű termelését, ebben az évben már két korábbi leállás is volt: az egyik váratlan, a másik pedig tervezett. A 2-es reaktor május 4-én, egy teljesítményelvezető transzformátorhoz tartozó szigetelő meghibásodása miatt állt le, ezzel párhuzamosan pedig május 10-én elkezdték az 1-es reaktor műszaki ellenőrzését, így az csak július 5-én kapcsolódott vissza az országos villamosenergia-hálózatra. Az 1-es reaktor ugyanakkor már 30 éves, ebben az évben jár le a szavatossági ideje, amit átfogó korszerűsítési munkálatokkal lehet újabb 25 évre meghosszabbítani. A tervek szerint a reaktor 2027 végétől 2030 júniusáig nem fog működni , ezalatt az idő alatt végzik el az (áfa nélkül) 2,9 milliárd eurós munkálatokat, így erre az időszakra Romániának alternatív energiaforrás után kellene néznie. Az atomerőmű bővítése is tervben van. Amikor az építését 1980-ban elkezdték a kanadai Atomic Energy of Canada Limited vállalat közreműködésével, még öt reaktort terveztek hozzá. Ceaușescu végül nem látta megvalósulni ambiciózus tervét , az első reaktort csak a rendszerváltás után, 1996-ban üzemelték be, a 3. és 4. tömb építését pedig még 1992-ben felfüggesztették, és csak tíz év múlva tértek vissza rá. Eleinte úgy volt, hogy kínai vállalat fektet be a projektbe, de végül az ipari kémkedés nemzetközi szinten felmerülő gyanúja miatt erről a Ludovic Orban vezette kormány kérésére 2020-ban lemondott a Nuclearelectrica . Még ebben az évben megállapodás született a román és az amerikai kormány között, azóta pedig különböző finanszírozási szerződéseket is aláírtak. A jelenlegi állás szerint a több mint 8 milliárd eurós beruházást amerikai, kanadai és olasz vállalatok valósítják meg, az új CANDU típusú reaktorok 2031-2032-ben kezdhetik a termelést. Beállítom Július utolsó napján rosszullét és hányinger miatt szállítottak a hatvani Albert Schweitzer Kórházba egy nyolcvanéves csányi nőt. Az asszony három éve fekvőbeteg volt, Alzheimer-kórral és demenciával küzdött, otthonában ápolta a családja – írja a Blikk . A kórházban ellátták, először haza akarták küldeni, de 12 óra után mégis bent tartották éjszakára. Másnap kora délután a zárójelentésben az állt, hogy egy egyszerű húgyúti fertőzést leszámítva jól van, otthonába bocsátható. Amikor a betegszállító megérkezett a család azzal szembesült, hogy a fekvőbeteg asszonyt ülve, leszíjazva szállították, és semmire nem reagál. Kiderült, hogy már nem él. A betegszállítók közölték, hogy ők nem tudnak újraéleszteni, a kiérkező mentők pedig már csak a halál beálltát tudták megállapítani. A Hatvani Rendőrkapitányságon indult közigazgatási eljárás a rendkívüli haláleset körülményeinek tisztázása érdekében – erősítette meg a Heves Vármegyei Rendőr-főkapitányság. A család jogi képviselője szerint eddig egy személyt hallgattak meg a rendőrök tanúként a családból. A betegszállító cég vezetője közölte, az eset kivizsgálása folyamatban van. A hatvani Albert Schweitzer Kórház főigazgatója szerint az eseményről augusztus 1-jén szombaton kora délután értesült az intézmény vezetősége, és már aznap rendkívüli vizsgálatot rendeltek el. Szedlák Miklós azt mondta, hogy eddig nem tártak fel olyan jellegű eltérést, amely a szakma szabályai szerint szükségessé tette volna a beteg azonnali, definitív osztályra történő felvételét. „Azonban az kérdés, hogy miképp nem láttak a szakemberek a vérképből és a röntgenből semmi rendelleneset” – tette hozzá. Az archiválásra került dokumentáció szerint az Intézmény rendelkezése a szállítás módját illetően „fekvő testhelyzetben” utasítás volt – szögezte le. https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachric.text: Fresha Accelerates European Expansion With New Warsaw Office and Appointment of Maciej Walczewski as General Manager for Eastern Europe Fresha, the world's most recommended AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, is accelerating its expansion in Poland with the opening of a new Warsaw office and the appointment of Maciej Walczewski as General Manager for Eastern Europe. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260723534553/en/ Maciej Walczewski, General Manager of Commercial in Poland Poland is a new and important market for Fresha, with a dynamic and rapidly growing community of beauty, wellness and selfcare businesses. The number of active partner businesses using Fresha in Poland has increased by 296% year on year, demonstrating the strong momentum behind the platform's expansion in the market. To support this growth, Fresha has moved to a larger office in Warsaw, establishing a new commercial operation from which to expand its team and strengthen relationships with Polish businesses and industry partners. From its base, Fresha plans to rapidly scale its commercial team across sales, account management and partner support, giving Polish businesses direct access to local market expertise at every stage of their growth. The company will also invest in dedicated marketing and brand-building activity, strategic industry partnerships, a stronger presence at beauty and wellness events across Poland, and continued product localization. Together, these initiatives will help Fresha accelerate marketplace growth and deliver an experience tailored to the needs of Poland's beauty and wellness industry. Walczewski's appointment marks the beginning of a new phase of dedicated, locally led growth. Working closely with Fresha's global leadership team, he will lead the company's Polish strategy, expand its presence in the market and help more businesses benefit from Fresha's integrated booking, payments, marketplace and business management platform. Maciej Walczewski, General Manager of Poland at Fresha, commented: "Poland has an incredibly ambitious and fast-evolving beauty and wellness industry, and Fresha has a major opportunity to support its continued growth. Our focus will be on building a strong local presence, listening closely to businesses and giving them the technology, marketplace reach and support they need to thrive. "We want to bring Polish SMBs and enterprise operators a platform powerful enough to reshape how the industry operates. By connecting partners to Fresha's complete ecosystem, we can help them run smarter, understand their customers more deeply and make better decisions through advanced configuration, customer tracking and in-depth reporting. "I'm excited to lead this next chapter and build a team that understands the Polish market, champions our partners and establishes Fresha as the platform of choice for beauty and wellness businesses across the country." Walczewski brings nearly 13 years of experience scaling technology and marketplace businesses across Central and Eastern Europe. Before joining Fresha, he served as Head of Sales for Uber, Agency Account Strategist for Google, Head of Sales for CEE at Ovoko, Country Manager for Poland at GoStudent and Vice President of Expansion at Packhelp. His appointment brings dedicated regional leadership to Fresha's global infrastructure, ensuring businesses in Poland and across the wider Eastern European region benefit from local market expertise alongside the scale, technology and capabilities of a leading global beauty and wellness platform. The expansion comes as beauty and wellness businesses increasingly seek technology that simplifies their operations while supporting sustainable growth. Fresha's unified platform brings together appointment management, integrated payments, customer retention, marketing automation and marketplace discovery, replacing the disconnected systems many businesses have traditionally relied upon. Through Fresha's marketplace, consumers can discover and book beauty and wellness services in real time, while businesses gain access to tools designed to improve efficiency, attract new clients and build lasting customer relationships. Poland's importance to Fresha reflects the strength and ambition of its beauty and wellness sector. From independent professionals and owner-operated salons to multi-location groups and fast-growing brands, businesses across the market are looking for flexible, scalable technology that can support every stage of their growth. William Zeqiri, Founder and CEO of Fresha, commented: "Poland represents an important growth opportunity for Fresha and is a key part of our long-term European strategy. It has a vibrant beauty and wellness industry, ambitious business owners and a strong appetite for technology that creates better experiences for both businesses and their clients. "Maciej brings the local leadership, marketplace experience and deep regional understanding we need to accelerate our growth. With him leading the charge, we're investing in our presence, strengthening our relationships with Polish businesses and building the platform of choice for the country's beauty and wellness industry." Poland now enters a new phase of locally led expansion within Fresha's global network. By combining dedicated regional leadership with Fresha's international infrastructure, the company aims to help Polish businesses simplify their operations, reach more clients and unlock new growth opportunities. About Fresha Fresha is the world's leading AI-powered booking platform for beauty and wellness, trusted by over 130,000 partner businesses across more than 120 countries. Its fully integrated ecosystem spans scheduling, payments, marketing, team management, and a global consumer marketplace, giving beauty and wellness businesses everything they need to operate, grow, and scale. The Fresha Marketplace connects millions of consumers with salons, spas, barbershops, and wellness studios worldwide, with over one million monthly downloads and more than $1.4 billion in monthly appointment value. To learn more, visit fresha.com. http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/23/.text: World / Europe One dead, several injured in Czech army helicopter crash Published: 23 Jul 2026 - 04:10 pm | Last Updated: 23 Jul 2026 - 04:10 pm AFP Prague: One person died and several were injured on Thursday when a military helicopter crashed in the Czech Republic with five soldiers on board, the army and emergency services said. "A Venom helicopter has crashed at the 22nd helicopter base in Namest nad Oslavou. Five soldiers were on board. Emergency services are currently deployed at the scene," the army wrote on X. Petr Janacek, a spokesman for the Vysocina regional rescue services, told AFP that one of the passengers was found dead and three were taken to hospitals in the region, two of them with "moderately serious injuries". A rescue operation was still under way, he said. No information was immediately available regarding the fifth soldier. The Namest and Oslavou airbase is located around 200 kilometres (125 miles) southeast of Prague. Police were informed of the accident at 12:11pm (1011 GMT), regional police spokeswoman Dana Cirtkova told the CTK news agency. Defence Minister Jaromir Zuna said the incident was "an immense tragedy that affects us all deeply", adding that an inquiry was under way to determine the cause of the crash. https://euobserver.com/225442/interview-.text: First published in Respekt. With influential Ukrainian MP Ivanna Klympush on the clash with Poland, Andrej Babiš’s trip to Ukraine and future coexistence with Russia. Ivanna Klympush-Tsintsadze (54) A Ukrainian journalist and politician, born in Kyiv. From 2016 to 2019 she served as deputy prime minister for European affairs in the government of Volodymyr Hrojsman. Since 2019 she has been a member of the Ukrainian parliament for the Petro Poroshenko Bloc. In the Ukrainian parliament you chair the committee for integration into the European Union. Will Ukraine become a member of the EU? Definitely. It will not be easy, the road will be bumpy, but I think it is out of the question that it would not happen! When do you think that will happen? There are many unknowns, so it is difficult to estimate. Those unknowns are on both sides, Ukrainian as well as European. What do you see as the biggest obstacle to accession on each side? I will start with the European side. I really appreciated that in 2022, after Russia launched its full‑scale invasion of my country, there was a geopolitical shift in the minds of many Europeans and a debate opened up about enlarging the Union to include Ukraine. Logically, this was accompanied by a discussion on how to reform the EU from within so that enlargement could actually happen. I have the feeling that these reflections on the necessary reform of the Union itself have somewhat subsided. That is a mistake; neither Ukraine nor any of the other candidate countries want to strive for membership for an indefinite period. The EU itself must also implement some changes in time, prepare more for our accession so that it becomes possible. The window of political opportunity for accession – and this is another complication – can also keep changing within the Union. In individual European states, political forces that will resist it can temporarily come to power. And what about Ukraine? What most complicates your path to Europe? Martial law has created, for some of our politicians in office, the temptation to roll back things that we thought had been protected since the Revolution of Dignity in 2014 and were taken for granted. I am talking about the decentralisation of power, about preserving certain freedoms, for example non‑interference with media freedom. This has to improve; we still have a number of domestic arrears to clear up. But I think everything is manageable. I was very pleased that this June the first round of accession negotiations with the EU was opened after Hungary, with its new government, lifted its blockage. This gives us new motivation, because we are in a real process. What would you say to Europeans who are afraid of your country joining the EU because of high corruption? https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/whe.text: Methodology Contact us Support Login Wheat commentary: Black Sea logistics risks continues to underpin prices Wheat prices were supported by strengthening energy markets, ongoing disruptions to Black Sea logistics and weather concerns in key producing regions. Continued uncertainty surrounding shipping through the Kerch Strait and the Strait of Hormuz helped sustain a geopolitical risk premium across agricultural markets. July 23, 2026 By Fastmarket team Agriculture Grains and oilseeds Wheat Escalating disruptions to Black Sea grain logistics continued to support wheat prices, as port damage, vessel cancellations and export uncertainty in Russia and Ukraine increased the premium for reliable export origins. Additional support came from concerns over US spring wheat production after the first day of the annual North Dakota crop tour estimated average hard red spring wheat yields at 46.0 bushels per acre, 8% below last year’s result. Wheat prices was further bolstered by increasingly bullish fund positioning on Euronext, where the net long in milling wheat climbed to its highest level since June 2022 as investors added long positions and reduced short exposure. EU wheat exports Meanwhile, EU wheat exports totaled 0.47 million tonnes by July 19, down from 0.86 million tonnes during the same period a year earlier, indicating a slower start to the bloc’s export campaign. However, ongoing logistical disruptions in the Black Sea continued to support demand for alternative export origins and helped offset the competitive pressure from European supplies. The soft red winter (SRW) September futures contract on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange rose by 4.17%, or $0.28 per bu, day on day to $7.06 per bu. The Kansas hard red winter (HRW) September futures contract rose by 4.26%, or $0.31 per bu, to $7.64 per bu. The Minneapolis hard red spring September futures on MIAX Futures Exchange rose by $0.24 per bu to $7.29 per bu and the Euronext milling wheat September futures rose by €10.00 per tonne to €244.75 ($279.29) per tonne. Australian wheat export values weakened in the nearby August loading window on Wednesday, with both APW and ASW assessments moving lower amid limited buying interest and a softer prompt market structure. FOB Australia APW 10.5% wheat for August loading was assessed at $279 per tonne, down by $2 per tonne day on day, while September loading remained unchanged at $280 per tonne. Market participants reported subdued demand for prompt shipment positions, with bids heard below assessed values. Similarly, FOB Australia ASW 9.5% wheat for August loading was assessed at $275 per tonne, down by $2 per tonne, while September values were unchanged at $275 per tonne. The decline reflected weaker nearby market indications and a lack of aggressive importer demand. In the Black Sea, selling indications for Russian 12.5% wheat were reported going lower at $238-$240 per tonne FOB Novorossiysk-Taman-Tuapse (NTT) for August-September loading, with bids lower by $2 per tonne day on day at $233 per tonne for August. An alleged deal was reported at $235 per tonne FOB NTT for loading in September, but Fastmarkets could not confirm any further details on it. Russian 11.5% wheat was reported $1 higher day-on-day at $236 per tonne FOB NTT for loading in August. Offers for Ukranian 11.5% wheat were seen again at $230-$233 per tonne FOB Pivdennyi-Odesa-Chornomorsk (POC) for August-September loading. Black Sea region update In the EU Black Sea region, on the Constanta-Varna-Burgas (CVB) market, limited Ukrainian logistics capacity has not yet translated into significant price support. Market participants said the main source of support currently comes from OAIC demand, with traders holding large OAIC-related positions paying premiums. Outside of this, the market remains focused on finding demand rather than competing for limited logistics capacity. There was a lack of offers on an FOB Constanța basis for 12.5% protein wheat. According to some sources, protein quality can be an issue in Romania this year, while others suggested there may still be outstanding short positions from the Saudi tender, supporting demand for 12.5% protein wheat. Selling ideas for 11.5% wheat on an FOB CVB basis were reported at €10 per tonne below the September Euronext wheat contract for August, also some offers were seen at $265-$266 per tonne FOB CVB. Offers for feed wheat on an FOB CVB basis were seen at €15 per tonne below the September Euronext wheat contract for August. Trading activity across European wheat markets remained quiet on Wednesday, despite a stronger performance in futures. Matif wheat extended gains as broader agricultural markets drew support from another sharp rise in energy prices and a threatening US weather outlook, while ongoing disruptions to commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Kerch Strait continued to underpin risk sentiment. In the physical market, activity remained limited. Sellers kept offers largely unchanged, showing little willingness to follow futures higher, while buying interest remained scarce, with bids largely absent from the market. Participants continued to monitor geopolitical developments and weather risks, but firm price ideas from both sides of the market left trading opportunities difficult to uncover. French 11% protein wheat was assessed at a premium of €2 per tonne to the September Euronext wheat contract for September loading. Polish 12.5% wheat cargo premiums were assessed at parity to the December Euronext wheat contract for September loading. Baltic FOB 12.5% wheat cargo premiums were assessed at a discount of €1 per tonne to the December Euronext wheat contract for September loading. The German 12.5% FOB wheat APM for September loading was assessed at €2 per tonne above the December Euronext contract due to a lack of fresh indications. No data was excluded. The German 11.5% FOB wheat APM for September loading was assessed at €2.50 per tonne below the December Euronext contract due to a lack of fresh indications. No data was excluded. US wheat cash markets US wheat cash markets moved higher on Wednesday, following the jump in futures markets as escalating attacks on infrastructure between Ukraine and Russia renewed concerns over Black Sea export flows. The heightened geopolitical tensions supported prices, with market participants closely monitoring the potential impact on grain exports from the region. The 11% FOB US Gulf HRW premiums were unchanged, with September at $1.50 per bu over the September Kansas HRW futures contract and October at $1.55 per bu over the December contract. The 10.5% FOB US Gulf SRW premiums were also unchanged, with September at 75 cents per bu over the September Chicago SRW futures contract and October at 85 cents per bu over the December contract. The 10% FOB Pacific Northwest soft white wheat market was higher, with September at $267 per tonne and October at $272 per tonne. Canadian western red spring 13.5% FOB Vancouver front-month premiums were unchanged, with September at 93 cents per bu over the September Minneapolis Grain Exchange (MGEX) futures and October at 85 cents per bu over the December contract. Canadian durum prices were steady, with 14.5% cargoes at $270 per tonne FOB Vancouver and $290 per tonne FOB St Lawrence. FOB Argentina wheat values were supported by broader gains in global wheat markets, as renewed Black Sea shipping risks, weaker US spring wheat conditions and crop downgrades in Russia and France reduced competitive pressure from key exporting origins. Higher Argentine new-crop wheat sales reflected improved market sentiment and favorable pricing conditions, while strong export commitments continued to underline demand for Argentina-origin material. For August, Argentina 11.5% wheat was assessed at $253 per tonne, and for September at $254 per tonne. Fastmarkets’ assessment for August and September increased both by $13 per tonne day on day. Fastmarkets’ assessment for feed barley FOB Argentina for August loading at Atlantic ports at $217 per tonne. New information was also disclosed for July, with offers at $225 per tonne and bids at $210 per tonne. https://www.mediafax.ro/english/educatio.text: Education union members refuse to participate in discussions on the new pay law The Federation of Free Education Unions (FSLI), the “Spiru Haret” Federation of Education Unions, and the “Alma Mater” National Trade Union Federation announced Thursday in a joint press release that they will not attend the discussions scheduled for today at the Ministry of Labor regarding the new pay law. The three federations state that they do not wish to legitimize, through their presence, a consultation they consider to be devoid of substance. “We will not use our presence to endorse a mere public relations exercise. The three federations have already conveyed their joint, well-founded, and detailed position during previous discussions. We cannot endorse stopgap solutions or minimal adjustments that do not genuinely address the problems we have highlighted. Given that the government and the Minister of Labor have already told us, bluntly and cynically, that this is the best they can do, our participation in today’s meeting would be completely pointless, serving only the public-image interests of those in power,” states the press release issued by the three labor federations. They accuse the current draft wage law of violating the regulations adopted by the government following the end of the 2023 general strike in education and argue that the government is not honoring the commitments it made to employees in the education system. “We draw attention to the fact that the current draft law flagrantly violates the very regulations adopted by the government upon the conclusion of the 2023 general strike. It is a display of hypocrisy and a total disregard for the commitments made to society. What the government is doing today is not only a violation of the law but a direct abandonment of the entire education system, proving once again that education is not a priority for the current government,” the education union representatives added. „Romanian lawmakers must choose between two options” In addition, the three federations are calling on Parliament to reject the current bill or to promote a version that reflects the importance of the work carried out by education personnel. “Romanian lawmakers must choose between two options: to refuse to introduce this pseudo-bill on salary reform or to promote a sound law in which education employees are classified according to the importance of the work they perform, as was the case with the draft developed by the Ministry of Labor in collaboration with World Bank representatives in 2024,” the joint statement further notes. On Tuesday, the judges of the Court of Appeals suspended the draft law on the remuneration of personnel paid from public funds, at the request of Sanitas. Thus, the draft published on July 17, 2026, can no longer be introduced or debated in Parliament. The judges found a clear appearance of illegality due to the lack of genuine consultation. In addition, the decision requires the government to resume official negotiations with public sector unions. The draft law on a unified pay scale is a reform that Romania has committed to under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR). https://www.baltictimes.com/taro__over_o.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Taro: Over one million individuals need to be added to the Schengen blacklist 2026-07-23 BNS/TBT Staff TALLINN – The European Union's attempts to restrict the issuance of tourist visas to Russian citizens are not hopeless, even though some member states continue to grant them, said Minister of the Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200), adding that Estonia's consistent pressure has led to a shift in both the rhetoric of member states and the stance of the European Commission. "I wouldn't want to say it's hopeless, because otherwise there would be no point in doing anything," Taro said on the Kuku radio program "Sihik," commenting on a discussion held a week ago in Dublin at a meeting of EU interior ministers. According to him, Estonia ceased issuing tourist visas to Russian citizens immediately after Russia launched its full-scale aggression in Ukraine and also denies entry to Russian citizens who hold tourist visas issued by any other Schengen country. "Estonia does not let them in: they are formally denied entry and sent back," the minister said, adding that this policy applies at both land borders and airports. Taro emphasized that Estonia's position has been clear from the start. "You cannot come to enjoy the Tallinn Christmas market while your country is bombing Ukraine." ESTONIA PRESSURES THE EU The minister noted that Estonia has consistently raised the visa issue at meetings of EU interior ministers. He said it was concerning that according to last year's Schengen barometer, nearly half a million visas were issued to Russian citizens in eight months, and the trend was increasing. "I said that this is completely unacceptable," Taro recalled. He explained that Estonia's criticism initially met with resistance from countries that issue the most visas, but their tone has since changed. "Their rhetoric has changed somewhat. It has become more apologetic; they claim that they are, in fact, conducting individual risk assessments," the minister said. However, he stressed that the problem has not gone away. "Ukrainians are dying every day, and you are letting Russian citizens travel just for fun, because the Kremlin's goal is to show that nothing significant has happened." ESTONIA WANTS TO EXPAND THE BLACKLIST According to Taro, there is a general consensus within the European Union that visas should not be issued to military personnel involved in Russia's aggression. "I have not yet heard a representative of any country say that this is not the right thing to do," he said. According to the minister, the discussion is primarily about which legal solution would be most suitable for different countries. Estonia's solution, Taro said, is to place individuals associated with the aggression on the Schengen blacklist. He noted that Estonia has already added thousands of names, with support expressed by Latvia, Lithuania, the Czech Republic, Finland, Sweden, and Poland. "We can add hundreds to the list with a single signature," the minister said, explaining that in some countries, adding each name requires a separate ministerial decision. In his view, the actual task is much larger. "We really don't need to add thousands to the list, but hundreds of thousands. In fact, there are over a million of them." https://www.baltictimes.com/study__diffe.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Study: Difference between cheapest and most expensive shopping basket in Estonia was over 12 euros 2026-07-23 BNS/TBT Staff TALLINN - In a July price comparison conducted by market research firm SeeNext, the cheapest shopping basket was found at Lidl, with the price difference to the most expensive basket being a significant 43 percent, or over 12 euros. According to the price comparison conducted by SeeNext at the beginning of July, Lidl was the most affordable among the retail chains surveyed. The average shopping basket at Lidl cost 28.02 euros, while at Coop, which proved to be the most expensive, the same basket cost 40.06 euros. This marks a price difference of 12.04 euros between the cheapest and most expensive baskets. The shopping basket used in the study consisted of 28 of the most commonly consumed products, with the cheapest available option for each item being selected at every store. The selection included various fruits like bananas and apples, vegetables such as potatoes and carrots, as well as dairy, meat, and grain products, and non-alcoholic beverages. "Lidl's goal is to offer products at a good price without compromising on quality. We focus on what people need every day and ensure that the daily shopping basket is as affordable as possible for our customers. A wide selection of private-label products, efficient work processes, a well-thought-out store concept, and close cooperation with producers help us keep costs under control and consistently offer customers a great price-to-quality ratio," said Liisa-Indra Pajuste, Head of Communications at Lidl Estonia. According to the study, Lidl offered the most affordable prices in nearly all categories compared: dairy, meat, grain, and beverage products. Notably, the price difference between the cheapest and most expensive retailer varied by category, ranging from 1.50 euros for beverages to 4.74 euros for dairy products. STUDY METHODOLOGY: During the study, SeeNext mystery shoppers visited stores of the six largest retail chains in Tallinn, Tartu, and Narva: Maxima, Rimi, Lidl, Selver, Grossi, and Coop. A shopping basket was compiled for the study, consisting of 28 of the most commonly used and cheapest everyday food items, including dairy products, meat, grain products, dry goods, fruits and vegetables, and beverages. https://www.baltictimes.com/over_800_you.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Over 800 young people apply to Estonian tech school expanding to Kenya 2026-07-23 BNS/TBT Staff TALLINN - The Jõhvi-founded programming school //kood is set to open its first on-site study program in Kenya this September. This week, 80 young people, selected from a pool of over 800 applicants, began an admissions program. Those who successfully complete it will secure a spot in the kood/Nairobi program, which starts in the fall. The program, supported by the Estonian Centre for International Development (ESTDEV), aims to cultivate the IT talent necessary for Kenya's rapidly developing digital economy. ESTDEV will fund 50 student placements in the kood/Nairobi program, which commences in September. "For Estonia, developing digital skills in Kenya is an opportunity to share our experience as a digital nation and in education, and to establish long-term collaborative relationships with Kenya's rapidly growing technology sector," said Katrin Winter, Head of Partnerships at ESTDEV. "Estonia's development cooperation aims not just for knowledge transfer, but for a partnership where our experience helps solve local challenges while simultaneously creating new opportunities for collaboration." According to Winter, Kenya is one of East Africa's most significant technology hubs, experiencing rapid growth in both the use of digital services and the demand for qualified specialists. "By supporting the development of local talent, Estonia is contributing to a stronger, more sustainable digital economy and laying the groundwork for new connections between Estonian and Kenyan businesses, educational institutions, and innovation communities," she added. Interest in the program surpassed all expectations, with candidates registering from across Kenya. Notably, nearly 40 percent of the applicants have no prior programming experience. The program is implemented by //kood, a technology school established in Estonia, whose graduates are employed by over 150 technology companies. The Nairobi program marks the school's first academic venture outside of Europe. ESTDEV supported the program through its Africa support fund, with a grant of 80,000 euros allocated for this new phase of the project. https://www.baltictimes.com/latvia_s_exp.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Latvia’s experience in countering malicious hybrid attacks is invaluable - Estonian minister 2026-07-23 LETA/TBT Staff RIGA - Latvia’s experience in countering malicious hybrid attacks is invaluable, said Estonian Minister of the Interior Igor Taro, who met with his Latvian counterpart Janis Dombrava (National Alliance) in Latvia this week. The Latvian Ministry of the Interior informed LETA that Dombrava hosted the Estonian Minister of the Interior during his working visit to Latvia. During the visit, the ministers discussed cooperation between the two countries in the areas of border security, migration management, civil protection and crisis management, as well as familiarized themselves with Latvia’s internal security infrastructure and the work of its internal affairs services. Dombrava noted that he and his Estonian counterpart are in agreement-the security challenges in the Baltics are becoming increasingly complex, which is why close cooperation between both countries is essential, and only by working together can we ensure a secure Baltic region and a strong external border of the European Union (EU). During the meeting, Taro emphasized that Latvia is not only Estonia’s closest neighbor, but also one of its most reliable allies. Latvia’s experience in countering malicious hybrid attacks is invaluable, and both the Estonian Police and the Estonian Border Guard are gaining valuable and irreplaceable experience by sending their officers to assist their Latvian colleagues in countering these deliberately created challenges. This cooperation will undoubtedly continue, Taro emphasized. On the first day of the visit, the Latvian and Estonian ministers of the interior visited the disaster management centers in Salacgriva and Saulkrasti, where they familiarized themselves with Latvia’s civil protection and crisis management system, local governments’ preparedness for emergencies and mechanisms for inter-agency cooperation. They discussed the role of disaster management centers in the civil protection system, coordinating cooperation between state and local government agencies and ensuring a rapid response to various types of threats. The ministers also visited the port of Skulte, where they discussed the port’s importance to the country’s security infrastructure. The visit continued in Mucenieki, where the ministers familiarized themselves with the work of the Asylum Seekers’ Center and the Detention Center for Foreign Nationals, discussing the management of migration flows, procedures for accommodating foreign nationals, and inter-institutional cooperation. Meanwhile, at the Riga Municipal Police Unified Command and Video Surveillance Center, the delegation learned about digital solutions for ensuring public safety and order, the use of video surveillance systems, and the coordination of rapid response operations. On the second day of the visit, Taro, together with Edvins Snore (National Alliance), Parliamentary Secretary of the Ministry of the Interior, visited the Latvian-Belarusian state border, the Silene Border Guard Unit, the Ludza Precinct of the State Police, the State Border Guard Special Operations Service Sigma, and the Terehova Border Control Point. During the visit, special attention was paid to the security of the EU external border, border surveillance infrastructure, the operational capabilities of the services, as well as the experience of the Baltic states and Poland in countering the migration pressure exerted by the Belarusian regime. Latvian officials thanked Estonia for the practical support provided to the Latvian State Border Guard during the period of enhanced border security operations. At the conclusion of the visit, the delegation met with representatives of the Aluksne Municipality to discuss current security issues facing border municipalities, civil protection and crisis management issues, as well as the challenges municipalities face in the current geopolitical situation. During the meeting, cooperation between the national government and local governments was also discussed, with a focus on strengthening resilience and preparedness for various potential crisis situations. https://www.baltictimes.com/lithuania_ex.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Lithuania expects Latvia to seek equipment, personnel for border security 2026-07-23 LETA/BNS/TBT Staff VILNIUS - Lithuanian Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas expects Latvia to request technical equipment, including thermal imagers, in addition to personnel to strengthen its border security. "We are in talks with the Latvian side. I hope they will express a need not only for physical capabilities and border guards on the ground (...) they also lack thermal imagers and night vision devices. Perhaps not as a gift, but we could lend them to strengthen their capabilities. There are many options, and I believe this is a conversation between our border leadership and theirs regarding specific needs," Katelynas told reporters on Thursday. The minister said specific assistance should be negotiated by border services rather than politicians to ensure solutions are tailored to Latvia's actual requirements. During the first six months of this year, secondary migration from Latvia to Lithuania surged from just over 300 to more than 1,200 foreigners. While Lithuania is already sending teams of border guards to assist Latvia, it does not intend to provide the full 100 officers requested. Since early July, nine officers from the Lithuanian State Border Guard Service, accompanied by service dogs, have been deployed to Latvia to help secure the border with Belarus. A second group of border guards followed on July 15. Saulius Nekrasevicius, deputy commander of the Lithuanian State Border Guard Service, said Latvia is currently the country most affected by instrumentalized migration. He reported approximately 150 attempted illegal border crossings in a single day, a figure comparable to the most difficult periods Lithuania experienced in 2021-2022. Nekrasevicius added that Lithuania cannot reduce its own security presence on the Belarusian border, meaning the scale of aid and the number of specialists sent to Latvia are being constantly coordinated with Latvia. The interior ministers of Lithuania and Latvia have also signed a cooperation agreement to combat crime, aimed at dismantling organized migrant smuggling networks. The rise in secondary migration has also caused problems for Poland. In July 2025, Poland reinstated checks at its borders with Lithuania and Germany, with controls currently in place until October 1. Katelynas said he discussed the situation in Latvia with his Polish counterparts, and border plenipotentiaries from Lithuania and Poland were scheduled to meet on Thursday to discuss improving inspection procedures. According to Katelynas, Latvia should negotiate directly with Polish border services for additional assistance. According to Lithjuanian State Border Guard Service data, more than 8,000 migrants have attempted to enter Latvia from Belarus this year, either being detained and returned or deterred on the Belarusian side. This figure is nearly nine times higher than the number of attempted entries into Lithuania from Belarus. Comments Related Articles Subscribe Log In Ads Please enter your username and password. Courtesy of the DOJ Naveen Athrappully Reporter 7/23/2026 | Updated: 7/23/2026 0:00 X 1 A man on the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters list, accused of a scheme to defraud Medicare of $547 million, was arrested by authorities on Monday. The foreign national, Khalid Satary, 54, owned and operated multiple diagnostic testing laboratories in the United States between 2016 and 2019 that billed Medicare for “expensive and medically unnecessary genetic tests,” the Department of Justice (DOJ) said in a July 21 statement. Satary is accused of conspiring with several patient recruiters and telemarketing services to generate unnecessary cancer genetic test samples that were reimbursed by Medicare at the rate of $10,000 to $20,000 per sample. To run the operation, Satary allegedly paid millions of dollars in bribes and illegal kickbacks to patient recruiters and doctors. The defendant was initially indicted in 2019. However, Satary was later released on bond, with the condition that he doesn’t work in the healthcare sector. While on bond, Satary allegedly conspired with labs in Texas to continue submitting fraudulent genetic testing claims to Medicare. A federal arrest warrant was issued against him in December 2022. However, Satary failed to appear for a court hearing and was believed to have escaped the United States. On July 20 this year, the defendant was arrested in the Middle East with a fake Mexican passport using a fake name. He was then transferred to U.S. authorities. Related Stories Lawmakers Propose $28 Billion Investment to Combat Fraud Groups Sue for Communication Records Linked to Somali Daycare Fraud Claims The Most Wanted Fraudsters list was announced by FBI Director Kash Patel last month. The White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud partnered with the FBI to compile the list, according to a June 19 X post from Vice President JD Vance, the task force’s chairman. The task force was established through a March 16 executive order signed by President Donald Trump, which said criminals and other individuals were exploiting various benefit programs intended to provide American citizens with a safety net. Trump ordered the task force to “coordinate and accelerate a comprehensive national strategy to stop fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.” One of those on the list, Said Abdullahi Ereg, surrendered to law enforcement on June 10, according to the FBI and federal prosecutors. Ereg is accused of laundering millions of dollars from a program that aimed to feed needy children during the COVID-19 pandemic. Another individual on the list, Herbert Leon Kimble, accused of $1.2 billion Medicare fraud, was arrested on June 11 in the Philippines. In its latest statement, the DOJ said that Satary has been charged with various fraud-related crimes, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and paying bribes and illegal healthcare kickbacks. He faces a multi-decade prison term if convicted. “The arrest of Khalid Ahmed Satary and return to the U.S. is the third Most Wanted Fraudster capture from this FBI and our partners in just five weeks—continuing the historic run of success for this new initiative,” Patel said in the statement. “This is another subject who exploited a program dedicated to helping our most vulnerable and instead stole for himself. Satary has been on the run since 2022, but we got him thanks to great work and coordination from the interagency and our overseas partners.” The Epoch Times was unable to reach Satary’s legal representative. According to the FBI’s website, Satary is one among nine individuals currently mentioned on the Most Wanted Fraudsters list. One of the individuals is a naturalized U.S. citizen of Somali origin wanted for allegedly being part of a fraud scheme that exploited the federal Child Nutrition Program during the COVID-19 pandemic. Another individual, a female from Jamaica, is linked to a scheme that fraudulently obtained more than $32 million from COVID-19 relief funds. A third person, a U.S. citizen, is wanted for alleged involvement in a mail fraud scheme in Georgia. The man allegedly defrauded at least $10 million from his victims. Meanwhile, on June 23, the DOJ announced that a coordinated enforcement action involving a whole-of-government approach led to the arrests of 455 individuals for their alleged role in healthcare fraud and opioid abuse schemes. The schemes, which involved more than $6.5 billion in false claims, posed “significant patient harm,” including death. Among the arrested were two Estonians connected to a $10.6 billion fraud scheme. Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty Images Morocco ‘Morocco feels emboldened’: Trump’s influence in spotlight after Ceuta disaster Washington-Rabat ties under scrutiny as questions swirl over what led to deadly influx into tiny Spanish territory Ashifa Kassam in Madrid Thu 6 Aug 2026 05.45 EDT Last modified on Thu 6 Aug 2026 06.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google T he cosy relationship between Washington and Rabat has long been flaunted by both sides, from Morocco’s announcement this year that it would be the first African state to join Donald Trump’s Board of Peace to the congratulatory message recently sent by Trump to mark King Mohammed VI’s 27 years in power. The latest example landed this week. As Spain grappled with the aftermath of the sudden influx – and swift return – of more than 70,000 people into Ceuta, Morocco’s monarch confirmed he had named a $1bn highway flanking the disputed territory of Western Sahara after Trump. The deepening ties have come under renewed scrutiny as questions continue to swirl over what exactly led to the deadly mass border crossing into the tiny Spanish territory in north Africa . “I think there’s enough evidence to hypothesise or claim that Morocco is behind this,” said Riccardo Fabiani, the north Africa project director for the International Crisis Group. “But there was no clear trigger for this, and this is what is puzzling for everyone.” 0:44 Migrants in Spain’s Ceuta enclave escorted back to Morocco – video Observers have suggested Spain’s recent rapprochement with Rabat’s archrival, Algeria, could have set off Morocco. But another, perhaps more plausible explanation pointed towards the US, said Fabiani. “It’s obviously impossible to demonstrate,” he said. “But in terms of plausibility, I don’t think it’s impossible to imagine that Morocco might have done something to earn brownie points with its allies, given that Morocco and this particular administration in Washington do have a very close, excellent relationship.” While Morocco had probably not “masterminded” the surge into Ceuta, he said, its relationship with the Trump administration – along with the Moroccan king’s desire to keep its claim to Ceuta in the spotlight – may have affected how it responded to fast-spreading online rumours about the Spanish border being thrown open. View image in fullscreen A young person is escorted by Spanish security forces after attempting to cross into Ceuta on Saturday. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters “For sure the Moroccan security forces were monitoring those conversations,” said Fabiani. “They saw that and there was probably some conversation where they decided to do nothing and see where this goes.” What followed made headlines across the globe as tens of thousands of people swam or waded across one of the EU’s two land borders with Africa. As Spain scrambled to cope, far-right voices seized on the images. In the US, the vice-president, JD Vance, and the state department blamed the influx on the Socialist-led government of Spain, while Trump warned that electing Democrats would make what happened in Spain “look small-time”. At no point did any of them mention Morocco or the potential role it might have played. Trump and his administration have long been open about the deep antipathy they feel for Pedro Sánchez, the Spanish prime minister, whose refusal to allow the US to use its airbases during the Iran war, rejection of the 5% defence spending target and vociferous criticism of Israel’s actions in Gaza have arguably made Spain the administration’s least favourite EU country. The American response seemed to be a triumph for Rabat, whose relationship with the US president traces back to his first term, when Morocco agreed to normalise ties with Israel in exchange for Trump’s recognition of its sovereignty claim over the disputed territory of Western Sahara . Since then, Morocco’s all-powerful monarch had doubled down on outreach efforts, said Fabiani. “The Moroccans have really made extra efforts to cultivate every single major decision-maker within the administration, including the president himself, to make sure that this administration will support, until the end, the Moroccan autonomy plan for Western Sahara.” A hint that the relationship could help Morocco lay claim to more than Western Sahara came in a recent US congressional report that appeared to be sympathetic to Morocco’s refusal to recognise Ceuta as Spanish territory, describing it as “Spanish-administered” rather than a part of Spain, as it has been since 1580. Days after the influx, interest in Ceuta remained heightened among those close to both Trump and the Israeli government, said Haizam Amirah-Fernández, the director of the Madrid-based Centre for Contemporary Arab Studies. “They haven’t stopped talking about Ceuta for several days in a row, which is quite striking.” View image in fullscreen Red Cross personnel distributing food at Trampolín beach in Ceuta this week. Photograph: REDUAN/EPA What had been laid bare was Rabat’s willingness to use “hybrid tactics to achieve political objectives”, said Amirah-Fernández, drawing a parallel with May 2021 when Rabat loosened border controls to allow more than 8,000 people to cross into Ceuta in a show of anger over Madrid’s decision to allow a Western Sahara pro-independence leader to travel to Spain to be treated for Covid-19. This time around, as nearly 10 times more people crossed into Ceuta, it set off a bout of finger-pointing across the EU rather than any kind of concerted effort to push back using the bloc’s status as Morocco’s largest trading partner and largest foreign investor. “The reaction of several governments in the EU was, in the end, what the White House was looking for – the erosion of solidarity between European partners,” said Amirah-Fernández. Senior officials in Morocco have pushed back against accusations it was in any way complicit. View image in fullscreen King Mohammed VI and Trump in 2018. Photograph: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty Images At the Rabat-based Moroccan Institute for Policy Analysis, there was little doubt that relations between Morocco and the US were in their “golden era”. Even so, the country’s approach to the Trump administration remained pragmatic, said Said Saddiki, a senior fellow at the institute. “Moroccan policymakers are well aware of President Trump’s transactional style and have sought to preserve Morocco’s strategic autonomy,” Saddiki said in an email, citing efforts to maintain partnerships with the EU, China and the Gulf states, among others. “The relationship with the Trump administration has strengthened Morocco’s international position, but so far it has not come at the expense of its relations with Spain or the European Union.” For Fabiani, the events in Ceuta served to underscore the perils of Europe’s reliance on north African states to control migration flows. “This has made Europe entirely vulnerable and dependent on the goodwill of a country like Morocco,” he said. “Morocco is a partner, but at the same time it has its own interests. This vulnerability was on show.” This weakness could become more of an issue as time passed, given Morocco’s perception that the issue of Ceuta remained unsettled, Fabiani warned. “And Morocco feels emboldened, and there is an administration in Washington that is willing to back it up,” he said. “I don’t think Europe is ready for what comes next because it could get much more complicated.” Explore more on these topics Morocco Donald Trump US foreign policy Spain Migration Refugees Middle East and north Africa news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

Photograph: Richard A Brooks/AFP/Getty Images Nintendo ‘Mamma mia!’: Trump tariffs refund ignites 53% profit spike at Nintendo Profit jump fuelled largely by unknown US refund amount as Japanese video game firm records quarterly sales drop Kalyeena Makortoff Thu 6 Aug 2026 07.11 EDT First published on Thu 6 Aug 2026 06.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nintendo has reported a jump in profits, as the Japanese game maker’s earnings were buoyed up by a long-awaited refund on Donald Trump’s tariffs. The company said profits surged 53.5% to ¥147.4bn (£694m) over the three months to June, substantially beating expert forecasts for ¥77.8bn. Nintendo said sales of its Switch 2 console, which was released last summer, “maintained strong sales momentum”, while popular games such as Yoshi and the Mysterious Book, Star Fox, and Pokémon Pokopia “performed steadily”. However, that did not make up for an overall drop in sales compared with the same period last year, with revenue down by 10% to ¥517.8bn. ‘Let’s-a go!’ The story of Nintendo – podcast Read more Instead, Nintendo said profits were aided by a refund on US tariffs, after the country’s supreme court ruled in February that Donald Trump’s sweeping “liberation day” trade levies were illegal. The Trump administration has refunded about $100bn from the tariffs charged before the court ruling, representing 60% of the total $165bn collected. Trump has continued to pitch tariffs as a solution for the US economy, bringing back domestic production, securing better trade deals and closing the deficit in the federal budget. Nintendo’s Tokyo-listed shares were up 2.87% on Thursday after the earnings release. The company filed a lawsuit weeks after the US supreme court ruling, demanding a full refund from the White House that would cover what it spent on tariffs, plus interest. While a refund now appears to have come through, Nintendo stopped short of confirming the full amount, at a time when it is still appears to be resisting calls to pass those refunds on to consumers. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning Preview latest after newsletter promotion Last month, Nintendo was hit with a class action lawsuit on behalf of customers , which claims the company hiked its prices because of tariffs but later benefited from the refunds. Nintendo’s lawyers described the lawsuit as “meritless”, and that the price customers paid represented “the purchase price of the goods they wanted and received.” Last month, Trump imposed a fresh round of tariffs on more than 80 countries, including Japan, in a move that is likely to pose further problems for companies such as Nintendo. However, a coalition of 25 US states are now suing the Trump administration over the levies , potentially opening the door to another round of refunds for beleaguered exporters. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP Australian immigration and asylum ‘Performative reductions’: Labor MPs and business groups urge Burke against sweeping immigration changes MPs say they are anxious for the government to avoid cuts to family and humanitarian visa categories Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Josh Butler and Krishani Dhanji Thu 6 Aug 2026 04.37 EDT Last modified on Thu 6 Aug 2026 05.09 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Major business groups have urged Labor to suspend its immigration changes and consult further with industry about how to get more skilled workers into the country, amid questions about looming Labor tweaks on permanent migration. With the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, delaying an anticipated immigration speech by at least one week, some Labor MPs say they are anxious to avoid major changes to the family and humanitarian visa categories, with one urging against “performative reductions” in migration in response to One Nation. But other Labor sources characterised Burke’s changes as tweaks to existing settings, with an expected focus on enforcement of existing rules and small pruning of various programs. “Tony’s doing an absolutely fantastic job of ensuring, that our immigration program which is so vital for us economically, vital for our vibrancy … the world’s most successful multicultural nation. But it must be properly calibrated,” said the energy minister, Chris Bowen. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Burke was to deliver a National Press Club address on Thursday about migration policy, but withdrew on Tuesday with a spokesperson telling media “some elements of the speech would not be finalised” in time. The ABC reported measures could include tougher family visa rules, capping backpacker numbers, or restrictions on asylum seekers. Burke’s office would not confirm media reports, and senior sources in the government remained tight-lipped on the changes. Some sources said they believed media and stakeholder focus on Burke’s speech had been overegged, characterising the changes as more “surgical” adjustments across multiple migration areas, and downplaying major changes to work, family or humanitarian visas. Another Labor source said they expected Burke’s speech would focus on how Labor plans to cut permanent migration to 185,000 a year – a target the government has cited in budget papers – rather than any cuts below that number. ‘Won’t happen’: One Nation Victoria leader’s comments raise questions about Hanson’s mass deportations policy Read more That figure includes about 132,000 skilled migration places and 52,000 partner and family visas. But potential cuts to either stream are already facing pushback from business groups and government members. Outside what will be detailed in Burke’s speech, his department recently announced that skilled migrants who were already in Australia would be given priority for permanent residency, which could help lower total migrant numbers, but also decrease the pipeline of available workers. The Minerals Council of Australia called on the government to “suspend skilled migration changes and consult industry” more closely on those changes. The MCA chief executive, Tania Constable, said the reforms would “make it harder for mining and other sectors”, raising fears about skills shortages and risks to project timelines, earnings and the economy. She said mining companies were already struggling to find workers. “Demand from these sectors for specialised skills is already growing faster than migration pathways can adapt, and industry is frustrated and impeded by slow updates, credential barriers and settlement constraints,” Constable said. The acting prime minister, Richard Marles, denied rumours of a disagreement with Burke in a cabinet meeting on Monday. 6:27 Barnaby Joyce suggests One Nation could welcome some refugees while barring other migrants – video “Migration obviously plays a really significant part in our economy, but it needs to happen at a sustainable rate,” he said. Pauline Hanson told News 24 that she didn’t care if employers groups thought a migrant crackdown “is going to affect their businesses”. “I don’t care. My concern is for those Australians that can’t get a roof over their head,” she said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion Labor MP Jerome Laxale told the ABC that Labor would strive to meet its 185,000 permanent migration target. “If that requires tweaks to our policy to do so, we just have to do that,” he said. The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry chief executive, Andrew McKellar, said it would be a “concern” if Labor was to trim working holidaymakers, while cutting family visas would also be a disincentive to attracting skilled workers. “The government should proceed with caution, we don’t want to shoot ourselves in the foot,” he said. “It would have a damaging impact if the government was to try to curtail those categories in a draconian way.” Master Builders Australia chief executive, Denita Wawn, added that the datacentres boom would need a new boost to construction workers, and called for tradespeople to be prioritised. “Migrant tradies ultimately contribute to far more homes than they consume, especially when they reside here over the long term,” Wawn said. Guardian Australia also spoke to several Labor MPs who said the government should tread carefully around partner visas, warning any cut to family categories would raise anxiety across communities. One MP said everyone including the government should stop being “hysterical” about migration numbers, and wanted to see firmer pushback by Labor against One Nation’s immigration rhetoric. “I am against performative reductions, I am in favour of steady migration … Getting skilled people in from overseas is imperative,” they said. “[Burke is] possibly driven by desire to be seen to be reducing migration rather than anything of substance.” Another MP said they would be concerned if the government reduced Australia’s humanitarian intake, while a third said cutting backpackers could be a way forward. One MP said there was confusion among those outside the cabinet who had not yet been advised of any changes. All said the issue was complex, and while reform across the system was needed, that the messaging was critical – especially amid the rise of Hanson and One Nation’s anti-immigration agenda raising fears in migrant communities. Photograph: Dan Kitwood/Getty Immigration and asylum Nearly 50 asylum seekers deported under ‘one in one out’ scheme have returned to the UK Figure raises questions about deal with France despite UK ministers insisting repeat arrivals will be removed Diane Taylor Thu 6 Aug 2026 09.32 EDT Last modified on Thu 6 Aug 2026 09.43 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Almost 50 asylum seekers deported using the “one in one out” scheme have been recorded as returning to the UK a second time, the Guardian has learned. It is believed that in addition to the returnees detained by the Home Office , an unknown number are likely to have arrived in the UK undetected. The scheme, which began last September, allows the UK government to return people arriving on small boats to France , in exchange for a similar number of asylum seekers being brought to the UK legally. The aim is to deter asylum seekers from crossing the Channel in small boats. The Guardian previously revealed that the first asylum seeker who returned to the UK a second time did so last October, a few weeks after being forcibly returned to France. But until now the number of people returning to the UK after forced return was not known. So far this year small boat crossings have reduced by about 43%. This fall is likely to be due to a variety of factors, including bad weather and a reduction in migrants arriving in Europe overall by about a third, as well as efforts by UK and French authorities to disrupt people smugglers. The rationale for sending a proportion of small boat arrivals back to France is that France is a safe country. Asylum seekers who have subsequently returned to the UK have argued that they faced threats from people smugglers in France, or feared being returned by French authorities to their home countries or to countries they passed through. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters Preview latest after newsletter promotion Has the UK government’s strategy on small boat crossings been effective? Read more About 4% of small boat arrivals have been returned to France so far under the “one in one out” deal. According to the Home Office, as of 30 June 2026, there were 1,117 individuals transferred to the UK and 1,087 individuals returned to France under “one in one out”. Officials say the treaty between UK and France has been amended so that second-time returnees to the UK will be once again returned to France. One asylum seeker who returned to the UK a second time in a lorry was eventually returned to France after spending five months in detention. He said he was accommodated for only a few days by French authorities. “There is nowhere for asylum seekers to go and be safe and have peace in Europe ,” he said. “I’m sleeping on the streets of Paris because France wants to send me back to Bulgaria where I was fingerprinted. I was better off in a UK detention centre.” Griff Ferris, of Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants, said: “People fleeing war, persecution and climate destruction are forced to take incredibly dangerous routes to cross the Channel and get to the UK because there is no other way. We must let everyone access the same safe routes to travel that are open to so many, like the daily ferries between Calais and Dover.” A Home Office spokesperson said: “Anyone looking to return to the UK after being removed under the UK-France agreement is wasting their time and money – and will be removed again. Under our payment by results returns agreement with France, we have removed more than 1000 illegal migrants from British soil. “Hundreds of enforcement actions, including arrests, investigations, and sanctions have been pursued against migrant smuggling networks since the election, and we’ve returned or removed almost 70,000 illegal migrants.” France’s interior ministry has been approached for comment.
